"""The Route Records to Topics guide, low-level API: a shop whose failed orders go to
their own topic.

It needs a Kafka broker on 127.0.0.1:9092: start one with `odctl up kafka-lite`. Run it
with `python complex_routing_low_level.py`, beside complex_routing_logic.py; it runs
for one minute. With ROUTING=router in the environment, it sends the records through a
function instead, which wins over the topic in the payload.
"""

import itertools
import logging
import os

from complex_routing_logic import custom_kafka_router
from desflow import (
    CapacityConfig,
    DistributionConfig,
    DynamicRealtimeEnvironment,
    DynamicResource,
    KafkaEgress,
    Sampler,
    SimParameter,
)

BOOTSTRAP = os.environ.get("KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS", "127.0.0.1:9092")
PARAMS = SimParameter(
    sim_id="Shop",
    arrival={"orders": DistributionConfig(dist="exponential", rate=0.5)},
    service={"packing": DistributionConfig(dist="constant", value=1.5)},
    resources={"packers": CapacityConfig(current_cap=1, max_cap=1)},
)


def payload_egress() -> KafkaEgress:
    """Sends each record to the topic its payload names, and creates the topics."""
    return KafkaEgress(
        bootstrap_servers=BOOTSTRAP,
        event_topic="shop-events",
        telemetry_topic="shop-telemetry",
        topic_policy="create",
        topics={"system-alarms": {}},
    )


def router_egress() -> KafkaEgress:
    """Sends each record to the topic a function picks."""
    return KafkaEgress(
        bootstrap_servers=BOOTSTRAP,
        topic_router=custom_kafka_router,
        topics={"shop-events": {}, "shop-telemetry": {}, "system-alarms": {}},
    )


def pack_order(env, packers, sampler, key, task_id):
    path_id = "Shop.service.packing"
    stats = env.stats
    queued = {"path_id": path_id, "sim_id": "Shop", "service": "packing"}
    env.publish_event(key, {**queued, "status": "queued"}, "pack_order", task_id)
    stats.task_queued("pack_order", task_id)
    with packers.request() as unit:
        yield unit
        env.publish_event(key, {**queued, "status": "started"}, "pack_order", task_id)
        stats.task_started("pack_order", task_id)
        yield env.timeout(sampler.sample(env.registry.get_config(path_id)))
        failed = task_id % 10 == 9  # every tenth order
        payload = {
            "status": "packing_failed" if failed else "packed",
            "__topic__": "system-alarms" if failed else "shop-events",
        }
        env.publish_event(key, payload, "pack_order", task_id)
        stats.task_finished("pack_order", task_id)


def orders(env, packers, sampler):
    gap = env.registry.get_config("Shop.arrival.orders")
    for number in itertools.count(1):
        yield env.timeout(sampler.sample(gap))
        env.process(pack_order(env, packers, sampler, f"orders-{number}", number - 1))


def run(until=60.0, egress=None):
    """Runs the shop unpaced into `egress`, which is `payload_egress()` unless given."""
    env = DynamicRealtimeEnvironment(factor=0)
    env.registry.register_sim_parameter(PARAMS)
    env.setup_egress([egress or payload_egress()])
    env.setup_stats("Shop", "minimal", interval=10)  # readings for shop-telemetry
    packers = DynamicResource(env, "Shop", "packers")
    env.process(orders(env, packers, Sampler(seed=42)))
    try:
        env.run(until=until)
    finally:
        env.teardown()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    run(router_egress() if os.environ.get("ROUTING") == "router" else payload_egress())

docs.title: Data at Scale
docs.text:
Generate a dataset of the size you name, such as a month of orders for 1,000 customers, as one Parquet file for each day, and check that it is complete. The run needs no wall-clock time: it takes as long as the machine needs to compute the records.

For the speed of one run, see Tune Performance. This page is about the size of the data and how to split a job that is too large for one run.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
• Write to Cloud Storage explains __path__ and how the sinks name their files.
  • Time and Pacing explains factor: 0 and logical_start_time.
  • Install the extra: pip install "desflow[parquet]".
  • The code runs in a folder of your choice. The files go to scale_output/, or to the folder in OUT. CUSTOMERS and DAYS set the size, and a small value for each is the quickest way to try the page, such as CUSTOMERS=20 DAYS=3.

docs.title: Set the Span
docs.text:
A run covers the period you want when it starts at the first day, runs without waiting, and stops at the last. factor: 0 removes the wait, logical_start_time and timezone fix the calendar the file names are built from, and run.until is the length of the period:

YAMLBuilderLow-level docs/snippets/yaml/data_at_scale.yaml:span
simulation:
  sim_id: Shop
  factor: 0
  random_seed: ${SEED:-42}
  timezone: UTC
  logical_start_time: "2026-01-01T00:00:00+00:00"

run: {until: "${DAYS:-30} days"}
docs/snippets/guides/data_at_scale.py:span
def new_shop() -> SimulationContext:
    """A shop that runs without waiting and starts on 1 January 2026, UTC."""
    return SimulationContext(
        sim_id="Shop",
        factor=0,
        random_seed=int(os.getenv("SEED", "42")),
        timezone="UTC",
        logical_start_time=datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc),
    )
docs/snippets/guides/data_at_scale_low_level.py:span
def new_env() -> DynamicRealtimeEnvironment:
    """An environment that runs without waiting and starts on 1 January 2026, UTC."""
    return DynamicRealtimeEnvironment(
        factor=0,
        logical_start_time=datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc),
        timezone="UTC",
    )

The period is 30 days unless DAYS says otherwise.

docs.title: Set the Volume
docs.text:
The number of records comes from how many entities there are and how often each one acts. This shop has 1,000 customers, and each orders after a gap of 12 to 36 hours, so a customer places about one order a day. count makes the customers, key gives each its name, and the gap is drawn again after every order. The month then holds about 30,000 orders. For a different volume, change CUSTOMERS, or the gap:

YAMLBuilderLow-level docs/snippets/yaml/data_at_scale.yaml:volume
arrivals:
  # Each customer orders about once a day: a gap of 12 to 36 hours, drawn again after
  # each order
  customers:
    dist: uniform
    low: 43200
    high: 129600
    spawn: place_order
    count: ${CUSTOMERS:-1000}
    key: {gen: sequence, start: "${FIRST:-1}", format: "customer-{}"}
docs/snippets/guides/data_at_scale.py:volume
def add_customers(app: SimulationContext) -> None:
    """One arrival for each customer, ordering about once a day (12 to 36 hours apart).
    A blueprint's `count` is one arrival here, each with its own key."""
    for number in range(FIRST, FIRST + CUSTOMERS):
        app.add_arrival(
            f"customer-{number}",
            "uniform",
            low=43200,
            high=129600,
            spawn="place_order",
            key=lambda n, number=number: f"customer-{number}",
        )
docs/snippets/guides/data_at_scale_low_level.py:volume
def add_customers(env: DynamicRealtimeEnvironment) -> None:
    """One process for each customer, ordering about once a day (12 to 36 hours apart)."""
    sampler = Sampler(seed=int(os.getenv("SEED", "42")))
    gap = DistributionConfig(dist="uniform", low=43200, high=129600)
    amounts = sampler.generator("tasks.place_order.payload.amount")
    sent = {"orders": 0}

    def customer(key):
        while True:
            yield env.timeout(sampler.sample(gap))
            amount = round(float(amounts.normal(40, 10)), 2)
            order = order_row(env, key, sent["orders"], amount)
            env.publish_event(key, order, task="place_order", instance=sent["orders"])
            sent["orders"] += 1

    for number in range(FIRST, FIRST + CUSTOMERS):
        env.process(customer(f"customer-{number}"))

keys takes a list of names instead of count and key, for entities with names you choose.

docs.title: Write a File for Each Day
docs.text:
__path__ in the order sends it to the file of its day, as Write to Cloud Storage explains. A Parquet sink writes one file for each batch, so a batch_size of 10,000 makes a file of up to 10,000 rows instead of one for every 500 records, the default. A file name is the path with an eight-digit hexadecimal suffix, such as 2026-01-01_a28fed01.parquet:

YAMLBuilderLow-level docs/snippets/yaml/data_at_scale.yaml:files
tasks:
  place_order:
    payload:
      # Numbered within the run, so the first customer of the run is part of the id
      order_id: {gen: sequence, format: "${FIRST:-1}-{}"}
      customer: {gen: entity}
      amount: {gen: normal, mean: 40, std: 10, decimals: 2}
      # The file of the order: the day it was placed, in the simulated calendar
      __path__: {gen: format_time, format: "${OUT:-scale_output}/%Y-%m-%d.parquet"}

egress:
  - type: Parquet
    # One file for each batch, so a large batch gives few, large files
    batch_size: 10000
    config:
      default_path: ${OUT:-scale_output}/other.parquet
docs/snippets/guides/data_at_scale.py:files
def add_files(app: SimulationContext) -> None:
    """A Parquet sink with a large batch, and an order that names the file of its day."""
    # One file for each batch, so a large batch gives few, large files
    app.add_egress(
        ParquetStorageEgress(default_path=f"{OUT}/other.parquet"), batch_size=10000
    )
    order = Template(
        {
            # Numbered within the run, so the first customer of the run is part of the id
            "order_id": {"gen": "sequence", "format": f"{FIRST}-{{}}"},
            "customer": {"gen": "entity"},
            "amount": {"gen": "normal", "mean": 40, "std": 10, "decimals": 2},
            # The file of the order: the day it was placed, in the simulated calendar
            "__path__": {"gen": "format_time", "format": f"{OUT}/%Y-%m-%d.parquet"},
        },
        name="tasks.place_order",
    )

    @app.task(name="place_order")
    def place_order(task_id):
        return order
docs/snippets/guides/data_at_scale_low_level.py:files
def setup_files(env: DynamicRealtimeEnvironment) -> None:
    """A Parquet sink with a large batch. One file for each batch, so a large batch
    gives few, large files."""
    env.setup_egress(
        [ParquetStorageEgress(default_path=f"{OUT}/other.parquet")], batch_size=10000
    )


def order_row(env: DynamicRealtimeEnvironment, key: str, number: int, amount: float):
    """An order that names the file of its day."""
    # The file of the order: the day it was placed, in the simulated calendar
    day = env.start_datetime + timedelta(seconds=env.now)
    return {
        # Numbered within the run, so the first customer of the run is part of the id
        "order_id": f"{FIRST}-{number}",
        "customer": key,
        "amount": amount,
        "__path__": day.strftime(f"{OUT}/%Y-%m-%d.parquet"),
    }

docs.title: Split a Large Job
docs.text:
One run keeps its entities and its records in one process. When a month for 1,000 customers is too much for one run, or too slow, run several shards, each as a separate process with its own part of the customers. Give each shard its own FIRST, CUSTOMERS and SEED, so that no two shards share a customer or a random sequence. They can write to the same folder, because every file name has its own suffix:

YAMLBuilderLow-level 
desflow run data_at_scale.yaml --var FIRST=1 --var CUSTOMERS=500 --seed 1 &
desflow run data_at_scale.yaml --var FIRST=501 --var CUSTOMERS=500 --seed 2 &
wait

FIRST=1 CUSTOMERS=500 SEED=1 python data_at_scale.py &
FIRST=501 CUSTOMERS=500 SEED=2 python data_at_scale.py &
wait

FIRST=1 CUSTOMERS=500 SEED=1 python data_at_scale_low_level.py &
FIRST=501 CUSTOMERS=500 SEED=2 python data_at_scale_low_level.py &
wait

Each shard writes its own file for each day, so a day has one file for each shard. The order ids start with the number of the shard's first customer, so they stay unique across shards. To split by period instead, give each shard its own logical_start_time and run.until.

desflow run --replications does not do this. A replication runs the model with no ingress and no egress, so it writes no files. It is for the spread of a result, not for data.

docs.title: Check the Result
docs.text:
Count the rows and the files of each day, and compare the total with the volume the model should give. Each customer orders about once a day, but the first order comes 12 to 36 hours in, so the total is about half a day short of customers times days. Save data_at_scale_check.py from Full Files and run it from the folder of the files:

docs/snippets/guides/data_at_scale_check.py:check
import sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

import pyarrow.parquet as pq


def check(folder: str, customers: int, days: int) -> int:
    """Prints the files and rows of each day and returns the total rows."""
    rows: Counter = Counter()
    files: Counter = Counter()
    for path in sorted(Path(folder).glob("*.parquet")):
        day = path.name[:10]  # the day in the file name, such as 2026-01-01
        files[day] += 1
        rows[day] += pq.ParquetFile(path).metadata.num_rows
    for day in sorted(rows):
        print(f"{day}  {files[day]} file  {rows[day]:>7} rows")
    # Each customer orders once a day on average. Its first order comes 12 to 36 hours
    # in, so the total is about half a day short of customers * days.
    expected = customers * (days - 0.46)
    total = sum(rows.values())
    print(f"total {total} rows, expected about {expected:.0f}")
    assert len(rows) == days, f"{len(rows)} days have a file, expected {days}"
    assert abs(total - expected) < 0.1 * expected, (
        "the total is far from the expected volume"
    )
    return total


if __name__ == "__main__":
    folder = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "scale_output"
    customers = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 1000
    days = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 30
    check(folder, customers, days)

python data_at_scale_check.py scale_output 20 3

2026-01-01  1 file        9 rows
2026-01-02  1 file       20 rows
2026-01-03  1 file       18 rows
total 47 rows, expected about 51

The check stops with an error when a day has no file, or when the total is more than 10 percent from the expected volume. After a sharded run, it counts the files of every shard in the folder, so the days show one file for each shard.

docs.title: Use Schema Serializers
docs.text:
Send orders to two Kafka topics, one as JSON checked against a JSON Schema and one as Protobuf, and read each back with the matching deserializer.

JSON Schema keeps a record as JSON and checks it against a schema before it is sent. Protobuf sends it as a compact binary message of a class generated from a .proto file. Either way, a consumer can rely on the shape of every record it reads. Both formats use the Confluent Schema Registry or the AWS Glue Schema Registry, and each topic can have its own serializer.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
• Use Avro and Pydantic shows the same steps for Avro, and Route Records to Topics explains __topic__, which this page uses to pick the topic.
  • The code publishes to Kafka and to a schema registry, so start both with odctl up kafka-lite. See Installation for the one-time odctl install. Stop it with odctl down kafka-lite --volumes.
  • Each serializer needs its extra: pip install "desflow[confluent]" for the Confluent Schema Registry, or pip install "desflow[glue]" for the AWS Glue Schema Registry. Both include kafka.

docs.title: Describe the Record in JSON Schema
docs.text:
As with Avro, the schema describes the whole record KafkaEgress sends, with your payload as value. The serializer raises SerializationError for a record that does not match, and a deserializer checks each record it reads in the same way. A blueprint reads the schema from a file, order_record.schema.json, which holds the same schema as this string:

docs/snippets/guides/json_schema_and_protobuf_serializers.py:json-schema
from desflow.connectors.egress.kafka import ConfluentJsonSchemaSerializer

# The schema describes the whole record KafkaEgress sends, with the order as its value.
json_schema = """{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "key": {"type": "string"},
    "task": {"type": ["string", "null"]},
    "instance": {"type": ["integer", "null"]},
    "sim_ts": {"type": "number"},
    "timestamp": {"type": "string"},
    "value": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "order_id": {"type": "integer"},
        "amount": {"type": "number"}
      },
      "required": ["order_id", "amount"]
    }
  },
  "required": ["key", "sim_ts", "timestamp", "value"]
}"""

json_serializer = ConfluentJsonSchemaSerializer(
    registry_url="http://127.0.0.1:8081", schema_str=json_schema
)

ConfluentJsonSchemaSerializer registers the schema as you wrote it, under the subject <topic>-value, on the first record of each topic. It checks a schema with no $schema as Draft 2020-12. It registers no references, so the schema must hold every definition it uses, and a $ref points only inside the schema. ConfluentJsonSchemaDeserializer resolves a $ref to a schema that the writer registered as a reference. Neither fetches a schema from a web address.

docs.title: Describe the Record in Protobuf
docs.text:
Protobuf sends each record as a message of a class that protoc generates from a .proto file. This file describes the same record as the JSON schema:

docs/snippets/guides/shop_record.proto
// The record KafkaEgress sends for an order, as the JSON Schema and Protobuf
// guide publishes it. Generate shop_record_pb2.py from it with the command on that page.
syntax = "proto3";

package com.desflow.shop;

message Order {
  int64 order_id = 1;
  double amount = 2;
}

// `optional` keeps a missing task or instance apart from 0 and "", as null is in JSON.
message ShopRecord {
  string key = 1;
  optional string task = 2;
  optional int64 instance = 3;
  double sim_ts = 4;
  string timestamp = 5;
  Order value = 6;
}

The code forms use the Python module that protoc generates. This command uses the protoc that grpcio-tools 1.85.0 bundles, which is protoc 35.1, in the folder that holds the file:

uvx --from grpcio-tools==1.85.0 python -m grpc_tools.protoc -I. --python_out=. --pyi_out=. shop_record.proto

The module checks the protobuf runtime when it is imported and refuses a runtime older than the protoc that wrote it. The header of shop_record_pb2.py names the oldest runtime that imports it: Protobuf Python Version: 7.35.1. For your own file, use a protoc whose header shows a version no newer than the protobuf you have installed. A blueprint cannot import a Python module, so it reads a descriptor file that protoc writes from the same .proto file:

uvx --from grpcio-tools==1.85.0 python -m grpc_tools.protoc -I. --descriptor_set_out=shop_record.desc --include_imports shop_record.proto

The serializer takes the generated class. It registers the file of the class under the subject <topic>-value on the first record of each topic, after the files that it imports. It builds the message from the record by field name and drops a key that the file does not have:

docs/snippets/guides/json_schema_and_protobuf_serializers.py:protobuf
from shop_record_pb2 import ShopRecord

from desflow.connectors.egress.kafka import ConfluentProtobufSerializer

# message_type is the class that protoc generated. The serializer registers its file.
protobuf_serializer = ConfluentProtobufSerializer(
    registry_url="http://127.0.0.1:8081", message_type=ShopRecord
)

docs.title: Serialize Two Topics
docs.text:
topics gives the settings of each topic, and its serializer names the serializer of that topic. A topic with no serializer uses the default, JSON. In a blueprint the serializer is a mapping with a type, here confluent_json_schema and confluent_protobuf, and the registry address.

YAMLBuilderLow-level docs/snippets/yaml/json_schema_and_protobuf.yaml:egress
egress:
  - type: Kafka
    config:
      bootstrap_servers: ${KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS:-127.0.0.1:9092}
      topics:
        orders-json:
          serializer:
            type: confluent_json_schema
            registry_url: ${SCHEMA_REGISTRY_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:8081}
            schema_file: order_record.schema.json
        orders-protobuf:
          serializer:
            type: confluent_protobuf
            registry_url: ${SCHEMA_REGISTRY_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:8081}
            descriptor_file: shop_record.desc
            message: com.desflow.shop.ShopRecord

docs.title: Publish Orders to Both Topics
docs.text:
Each packed order's finished event is the order record, and it names its topic with __topic__. In this shop the orders alternate between the formats, so one run shows both. The queued and started events name no topic, so they go to sim-events as JSON.

YAMLBuilderLow-level docs/snippets/yaml/json_schema_and_protobuf.yaml:shop
resources:
  packers: {current_cap: 1, max_cap: 1}

services:
  packing: {dist: constant, value: 1.5}

arrivals:
  orders: {dist: exponential, rate: 0.5, spawn: pack_order}

tasks:
  pack_order:
    service: packing
    resource: packers
    payload:
      # Orders alternate between the two formats, so one run shows both
      __topic__:
        gen: when
        condition: "process.instance % 2 == 1"
        then: orders-protobuf
        else: orders-json
      order_id: {gen: expr, expr: process.instance}
      amount: 19.99
docs/snippets/guides/json_schema_and_protobuf.py:shop
app = (
    SimulationContext(sim_id="Shop", factor=0, random_seed=42)
    .add_resource("packers", current_cap=1, max_cap=1)
    .add_service("packing", dist="constant", value=1.5)
    .add_arrival("orders", dist="exponential", rate=0.5)
    .add_egress(egress)  # orders as JSON Schema or Protobuf, the rest as JSON
)


@app.task(service_id="packing", resource_id="packers")
def pack_order(task_id: int, entity):
    # Orders alternate between the two formats, so one run shows both
    topic = "orders-protobuf" if task_id % 2 else "orders-json"
    return {"__topic__": topic, "order_id": task_id, "amount": 19.99}


@app.arrival_loop("orders")
def orders(context: SimulationContext):
    while True:
        order = yield context.wait_for_arrival("orders")
        context.spawn(pack_order(context.next_instance("pack_order"), entity=order))

shop takes the sinks as an argument, and the script passes it [egress]:

docs/snippets/guides/json_schema_and_protobuf_low_level.py:shop
def pack_order(env, packers, sampler, key, task_id):
    path_id = "Shop.service.packing"
    env.publish_event(
        key,
        {
            "path_id": path_id,
            "sim_id": "Shop",
            "service": "packing",
            "status": "queued",
        },
        "pack_order",
        task_id,
    )
    with packers.request() as unit:
        yield unit
        env.publish_event(
            key,
            {
                "path_id": path_id,
                "sim_id": "Shop",
                "service": "packing",
                "status": "started",
            },
            "pack_order",
            task_id,
        )
        yield env.timeout(sampler.sample(env.registry.get_config(path_id)))
        # Orders alternate between the two formats, so one run shows both
        topic = "orders-protobuf" if task_id % 2 else "orders-json"
        order = {"__topic__": topic, "order_id": task_id, "amount": 19.99}
        env.publish_event(key, order, "pack_order", task_id)


def orders(env, packers, sampler):
    gap = env.registry.get_config("Shop.arrival.orders")
    for number in itertools.count(1):
        yield env.timeout(sampler.sample(gap))
        env.process(pack_order(env, packers, sampler, f"orders-{number}", number - 1))


def shop(sinks: list, factor: float = 0.0) -> DynamicRealtimeEnvironment:
    """The shop, publishing to the sinks given."""
    env = DynamicRealtimeEnvironment(factor=factor)
    env.registry.register_sim_parameter(PARAMS)
    env.setup_egress(sinks)
    packers = DynamicResource(env, "Shop", "packers")
    env.process(orders(env, packers, Sampler(seed=42)))
    return env

docs.title: Use the AWS Glue Schema Registry
docs.text:
The same two formats work with an AWS Glue Schema Registry. The Glue classes need desflow[glue]; the rest of this page needs only desflow[confluent], so this function builds the Glue serializers only when it is called. They replace the Confluent ones in topics. In a blueprint the types are glue_json_schema and glue_protobuf, with the key registry_name for the registry and the key boto3 for the arguments of boto3.client, such as region_name. The classes take the same as keyword arguments (region_name="us-east-1"). Four rules differ from the Confluent classes:

  • GlueProtobufSerializer takes one more argument, schema_str: the text of the .proto file, because Glue stores the text and protobuf cannot print it from the generated class. The text must declare the same messages, in the same file, as message_type. In a blueprint it is the key schema_file.
  • GlueJsonSchemaSerializer compiles the schema with fastjsonschema when you build it, so a $ref to another document is fetched at that point.
  • GlueJsonSchemaSerializer fills in the default of a property that a record leaves out.
  • Glue checks a new version of a schema against the schema's compatibility mode before it is available. Both serializers wait for it: up to 10 checks, 3 seconds apart, which is about 30 seconds. If the version is still pending after that, the serializer raises an error that names the version.
YAMLBuilderLow-level docs/snippets/yaml/json_schema_and_protobuf_glue.yaml:egress
egress:
  - type: Kafka
    config:
      bootstrap_servers: ${KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS}
      topics:
        orders-json:
          serializer:
            type: glue_json_schema
            registry_name: shop
            schema_file: order_record.schema.json
            boto3: {region_name: us-east-1}  # passed to boto3.client
        orders-protobuf:
          serializer:
            type: glue_protobuf
            registry_name: shop
            descriptor_file: shop_record.desc
            message: com.desflow.shop.ShopRecord
            schema_file: shop_record.proto  # the text of the .proto file
            boto3: {region_name: us-east-1}
docs/snippets/guides/json_schema_and_protobuf_serializers.py:glue
def glue_serializers():
    """The same two formats for an AWS Glue Schema Registry; they need `desflow[glue]`."""
    from pathlib import Path

    from desflow.connectors.egress.kafka import (
        GlueJsonSchemaSerializer,
        GlueProtobufSerializer,
    )

    glue_json = GlueJsonSchemaSerializer(
        registry_name="shop", schema_str=json_schema, region_name="us-east-1"
    )
    # Glue stores the text of the .proto file, so the serializer takes it as schema_str.
    # It must declare the same messages as message_type.
    glue_protobuf = GlueProtobufSerializer(
        registry_name="shop",
        message_type=ShopRecord,
        schema_str=Path(__file__).with_name("shop_record.proto").read_text(),
        region_name="us-east-1",
    )
    return glue_json, glue_protobuf


def glue_egress():
    """The egress of the shop, sending the two order topics through the Glue serializers."""
    import os

    from desflow import KafkaEgress

    glue_json, glue_protobuf = glue_serializers()
    return KafkaEgress(
        bootstrap_servers=os.environ.get("KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS", "127.0.0.1:9092"),
        topics={
            "orders-json": {"serializer": glue_json},
            "orders-protobuf": {"serializer": glue_protobuf},
        },
    )

Pass glue_egress() to add_egress in place of the egress above.

docs.title: Read the Records Back
docs.text:
A consumer reads each order topic with the deserializer of its format. read_order takes the topic and the value of one message, from any Kafka consumer, and returns the record that was sent. Each deserializer fetches the schema that a message names from the registry. ConfluentJsonSchemaDeserializer checks every record against it, and ConfluentProtobufDeserializer decodes the message as message_type. For a Glue registry, GlueJsonSchemaDeserializer("shop", region_name="us-east-1") and GlueProtobufDeserializer("shop", ShopRecord, region_name="us-east-1") take their place: the registry name, for Protobuf the message class, and the arguments of boto3.client.

docs/snippets/guides/json_schema_and_protobuf_serializers.py:read-back
from desflow.connectors.ingress.kafka import (
    ConfluentJsonSchemaDeserializer,
    ConfluentProtobufDeserializer,
    MessageDeserializer,
)

# A consumer of the order topics reads each one with the deserializer of its format.
order_readers: dict[str, MessageDeserializer] = {
    "orders-json": ConfluentJsonSchemaDeserializer(
        registry_url="http://127.0.0.1:8081"
    ),
    "orders-protobuf": ConfluentProtobufDeserializer(
        registry_url="http://127.0.0.1:8081", message_type=ShopRecord
    ),
}


def read_order(topic: str, payload: bytes) -> dict:
    """Decodes one message of an order topic into the record that was sent."""
    return order_readers[topic].deserialize(topic, payload)

docs.title: Check the Result
docs.text:
Run desflow run json_schema_and_protobuf.yaml, python json_schema_and_protobuf.py or python json_schema_and_protobuf_low_level.py while kafka-lite is up, beside the files of the page. Each runs for one simulated minute and ends at once. Each form sends 10 orders to orders-json and 10 to orders-protobuf, and the other events to sim-events as JSON.

To read the first order of each topic back, run the serializers file after a shop has run. It prints what read_order decodes:

docs/snippets/guides/json_schema_and_protobuf_serializers.py:check
import asyncio

from aiokafka import AIOKafkaConsumer


async def show_first_order(topic: str) -> None:
    """Prints the first order of a topic, decoded by the reader of its format."""
    consumer = AIOKafkaConsumer(
        topic, bootstrap_servers="127.0.0.1:9092", auto_offset_reset="earliest"
    )
    await consumer.start()
    try:
        message = await asyncio.wait_for(consumer.getone(), timeout=10)
        print(topic, read_order(topic, message.value))
    finally:
        await consumer.stop()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    for topic in order_readers:
        asyncio.run(show_first_order(topic))

python json_schema_and_protobuf_serializers.py

orders-json {'sim_ts': 2.1283113312939435, 'timestamp': '2026-11-09T00:00:00.000+00:00', 'key': 'orders-1', 'task': 'pack_order', 'instance': 0, 'value': {'order_id': 0, 'amount': 19.99}}
orders-protobuf {'key': 'orders-2', 'task': 'pack_order', 'instance': '1', 'sim_ts': 6.434338901219139, 'timestamp': '2026-11-09T00:00:00.000+00:00', 'value': {'order_id': '1', 'amount': 19.99}}

The timestamp is the clock time of your run. A 64 bit integer field of Protobuf, such as order_id and instance, comes back from a deserializer as a string, so the Protobuf record shows '1' for order_id and instance where the JSON record shows numbers.

docs.title: Full Files
docs.text:
Every code form uses the serializers in json_schema_and_protobuf_serializers.py, which builds no shop, so keep the files in one folder.

Full files docs/snippets/guides/json_schema_and_protobuf_serializers.py
"""The serializers and order readers of the Use Schema Serializers page.

The code forms of the shop import the serializers from this file:
json_schema_and_protobuf.py (builder) and json_schema_and_protobuf_low_level.py. It builds
no simulation. shop_record.proto and shop_record_pb2.py, generated from it, must be beside
this file. It needs a Kafka broker and a schema registry: start both with
`odctl up kafka-lite`.

After a shop has run, `python json_schema_and_protobuf_serializers.py` reads the first
order of each order topic back.
"""

# Each section carries its own imports, as the page shows it.
# ruff: noqa: E402

# The schema describes the whole record KafkaEgress sends, with the order as its value.
json_schema = """{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "key": {"type": "string"},
    "task": {"type": ["string", "null"]},
    "instance": {"type": ["integer", "null"]},
    "sim_ts": {"type": "number"},
    "timestamp": {"type": "string"},
    "value": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "order_id": {"type": "integer"},
        "amount": {"type": "number"}
      },
      "required": ["order_id", "amount"]
    }
  },
  "required": ["key", "sim_ts", "timestamp", "value"]
}"""

json_serializer = ConfluentJsonSchemaSerializer(
    registry_url="http://127.0.0.1:8081", schema_str=json_schema
)


from shop_record_pb2 import ShopRecord

from desflow.connectors.egress.kafka import ConfluentProtobufSerializer

# message_type is the class that protoc generated. The serializer registers its file.
protobuf_serializer = ConfluentProtobufSerializer(
    registry_url="http://127.0.0.1:8081", message_type=ShopRecord
)

"""The shop of the Use Schema Serializers page, built with the builder API.

The shop publishes each packed order as JSON Schema or Protobuf and every other record as
JSON. It needs a Kafka broker and a schema registry: start both with `odctl up kafka-lite`,
then run `python json_schema_and_protobuf.py`. json_schema_and_protobuf.yaml and
json_schema_and_protobuf_low_level.py are the same shop in YAML and the low-level API.
The code forms import the serializers of json_schema_and_protobuf_serializers.py, which
must be beside them.
"""

# ruff: noqa: E402

import logging
import os

from json_schema_and_protobuf_serializers import json_serializer, protobuf_serializer

from desflow import KafkaEgress, SimulationContext

egress = KafkaEgress(
    bootstrap_servers=os.environ.get("KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS", "127.0.0.1:9092"),
    topics={
        "orders-json": {"serializer": json_serializer},
        "orders-protobuf": {"serializer": protobuf_serializer},
    },
)

app = (
    SimulationContext(sim_id="Shop", factor=0, random_seed=42)
    .add_resource("packers", current_cap=1, max_cap=1)
    .add_service("packing", dist="constant", value=1.5)
    .add_arrival("orders", dist="exponential", rate=0.5)
    .add_egress(egress)  # orders as JSON Schema or Protobuf, the rest as JSON
)


@app.task(service_id="packing", resource_id="packers")
def pack_order(task_id: int, entity):
    # Orders alternate between the two formats, so one run shows both
    topic = "orders-protobuf" if task_id % 2 else "orders-json"
    return {"__topic__": topic, "order_id": task_id, "amount": 19.99}


@app.arrival_loop("orders")
def orders(context: SimulationContext):
    while True:
        order = yield context.wait_for_arrival("orders")
        context.spawn(pack_order(context.next_instance("pack_order"), entity=order))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    app.run(until="1 min")

"""The Use Schema Serializers guide, low-level API: each packed order publishes
an order record, sent to orders-json as JSON Schema or to orders-protobuf as Protobuf, and
every other record goes to its topic as JSON.

The serializers are those of json_schema_and_protobuf_serializers.py, which must be
beside this script, with shop_record.proto and shop_record_pb2.py. It needs a Kafka
broker and a schema registry: start both with `odctl up kafka-lite`, then run
`python json_schema_and_protobuf_low_level.py`.
"""

import itertools
import logging
import os

from json_schema_and_protobuf_serializers import json_serializer, protobuf_serializer

from desflow import (
    CapacityConfig,
    DistributionConfig,
    DynamicRealtimeEnvironment,
    DynamicResource,
    KafkaEgress,
    Sampler,
    SimParameter,
)

PARAMS = SimParameter(
    sim_id="Shop",
    arrival={"orders": DistributionConfig(dist="exponential", rate=0.5)},
    service={"packing": DistributionConfig(dist="constant", value=1.5)},
    resources={"packers": CapacityConfig(current_cap=1, max_cap=1)},
)


egress = KafkaEgress(
    bootstrap_servers=os.environ.get("KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS", "127.0.0.1:9092"),
    topics={
        "orders-json": {"serializer": json_serializer},
        "orders-protobuf": {"serializer": protobuf_serializer},
    },
)


def pack_order(env, packers, sampler, key, task_id):
    path_id = "Shop.service.packing"
    env.publish_event(
        key,
        {
            "path_id": path_id,
            "sim_id": "Shop",
            "service": "packing",
            "status": "queued",
        },
        "pack_order",
        task_id,
    )
    with packers.request() as unit:
        yield unit
        env.publish_event(
            key,
            {
                "path_id": path_id,
                "sim_id": "Shop",
                "service": "packing",
                "status": "started",
            },
            "pack_order",
            task_id,
        )
        yield env.timeout(sampler.sample(env.registry.get_config(path_id)))
        # Orders alternate between the two formats, so one run shows both
        topic = "orders-protobuf" if task_id % 2 else "orders-json"
        order = {"__topic__": topic, "order_id": task_id, "amount": 19.99}
        env.publish_event(key, order, "pack_order", task_id)


def orders(env, packers, sampler):
    gap = env.registry.get_config("Shop.arrival.orders")
    for number in itertools.count(1):
        yield env.timeout(sampler.sample(gap))
        env.process(pack_order(env, packers, sampler, f"orders-{number}", number - 1))


def shop(sinks: list, factor: float = 0.0) -> DynamicRealtimeEnvironment:
    """The shop, publishing to the sinks given."""
    env = DynamicRealtimeEnvironment(factor=factor)
    env.registry.register_sim_parameter(PARAMS)
    env.setup_egress(sinks)
    packers = DynamicResource(env, "Shop", "packers")
    env.process(orders(env, packers, Sampler(seed=42)))
    return env


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(
        level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s [%(asctime)s] %(message)s"
    )
    env = shop([egress])  # orders as JSON Schema or Protobuf, the rest as JSON
    try:
        env.run(until=60)
    finally:
        env.teardown()

docs.title: Connect to Secure Kafka
docs.text:
Publish a simulation's events to a Kafka cluster that needs SASL, mutual TLS or Amazon MSK IAM, by passing the security settings in the sink's config.

The Kafka connectors pass any setting they do not use themselves to the Kafka client underneath, aiokafka, so SASL, mTLS, OAuth and AWS IAM work without code of your own. KafkaAdminConnector passes its settings to the aiokafka client of each method: the admin client for create_topics, the producer for send_config and the consumer for collect_data. Each setting must be one that client takes.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
• Install the Kafka connectors: pip install "desflow[kafka]".
  • Egress and Ingress explain the Kafka connectors without security.
  • Every example here connects to a managed or secured cluster. No odctl profile runs a secured broker, so the shop needs a cluster of your own, such as Confluent Cloud for SASL. To try the connectors locally without security, start a broker with odctl up kafka-lite and see Installation.

docs.title: Connect with SASL
docs.text:
For Confluent Cloud, or any cluster that uses SASL PLAIN or SCRAM, pass security_protocol, sasl_mechanism and the credentials. The address and the credentials come from variables, so no secret is in the file. With no topic_router, KafkaEgress creates sim-events and sim-telemetry when it starts, and passes the security settings to the admin client that creates them.

This simulation publishes its events through a SASL sink:

YAMLBuilderLow-level docs/snippets/yaml/kafka_security.yaml:shop
simulation: {sim_id: Shop, factor: 0, random_seed: 42}

resources:
  packers: {current_cap: 1, max_cap: 1}

services:
  packing: {dist: constant, value: 1.5}

arrivals:
  orders: {dist: exponential, rate: 0.5, spawn: pack_order}

tasks:
  pack_order:
    service: packing
    resource: packers
    payload: {event_type: order_packed}

egress:
  - type: Kafka
    config:
      bootstrap_servers:
        ${KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS:-pkc-xxxx.us-east-1.aws.confluent.cloud:9092}
      # Passed as they are to the Kafka client
      security_protocol: SASL_SSL
      sasl_mechanism: PLAIN  # or SCRAM-SHA-512
      sasl_plain_username: ${KAFKA_API_KEY:-<YOUR_API_KEY>}
      sasl_plain_password: ${KAFKA_API_SECRET:-<YOUR_API_SECRET>}

run: {until: 1 min}

import os
from typing import Any, Dict

from desflow import KafkaEgress


def sasl_connection() -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """The settings of a cluster that uses SASL. The environment holds the credentials."""
    return dict(
        bootstrap_servers=os.environ["KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS"],
        # Passed as they are to the Kafka client
        security_protocol="SASL_SSL",
        sasl_mechanism="PLAIN",  # or SCRAM-SHA-512
        sasl_plain_username=os.environ["KAFKA_API_KEY"],
        sasl_plain_password=os.environ["KAFKA_API_SECRET"],
    )


def sasl_egress() -> KafkaEgress:
    """The egress of a cluster that uses SASL."""
    return KafkaEgress(**sasl_connection())

docs.title: Connect with mTLS
docs.text:
For a cluster that requires mutual TLS, ssl takes the certificate files: cafile, certfile, keyfile and, for an encrypted key, password. The sink builds the SSL context from them with aiokafka.helpers.create_ssl_context, so one setting serves the sink and the other Kafka connectors. Set security_protocol to SSL as well. The Builder and Low-level forms run the same shop as the SASL step with this egress: build(mtls_egress()) and shop([mtls_egress()]).

    config:
      bootstrap_servers: ${KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS}
      security_protocol: SSL
      # The arguments of aiokafka.helpers.create_ssl_context
      ssl:
        cafile: ${KAFKA_CA_FILE}
        certfile: ${KAFKA_CERT_FILE}
        keyfile: ${KAFKA_KEY_FILE}

docs.title: Connect to AWS MSK
docs.text:
Amazon MSK with IAM access control uses sasl_mechanism OAUTHBEARER with a token provider. sasl_oauth_token_provider: {type: aws_msk_iam, region: <region>} builds one that signs a token with the AWS credentials of your environment, or the EC2 or EKS role. It needs the package aws-msk-iam-sasl-signer-python, which you install yourself. Set security_protocol to SASL_SSL as well. For Okta, Auth0 or another single sign-on provider, pass your own subclass of aiokafka.abc.AbstractTokenProvider with an async token() in the Builder and Low-level forms. The Builder and Low-level forms run the same shop as the SASL step with this egress: build(msk_egress()) and shop([msk_egress()]).

docs.title: Connect to a Secured Schema Registry
docs.text:
A schema registry that needs a user name, a certificate or a proxy takes its own settings, apart from the Kafka ones. The Confluent serializers (confluent_avro, confluent_json_schema and confluent_protobuf) and the Confluent deserializers take these arguments:

  • auth: a user name and a password.
  • verify: true, false, the path of a CA file or directory, or in code an ssl.SSLContext. A YAML blueprint cannot write a context.
  • cert: a client certificate file, or a list of the certificate file, the key file and the key password.
  • headers: extra headers, such as a bearer token.
  • proxy: the URL of a proxy.
  • timeout: the seconds each step of a request (connecting, sending, reading) may take. The default is 10. null waits without a limit.
  • max_retries: how many times a request is repeated after a timeout or another transport error (3 by default).

This shop sends its predictions to ml-predictions as Avro, as Use Avro and Pydantic does, through a registry with all of these settings. The Builder and Low-level forms need avro_and_pydantic_models.py of that page beside them.

YAMLBuilderLow-level docs/snippets/yaml/kafka_security_registry.yaml:egress
egress:
  - type: Kafka
    config:
      bootstrap_servers: ${KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS}
      topics:
        ml-predictions:
          serializer:
            type: confluent_avro
            registry_url: ${SCHEMA_REGISTRY_URL}
            schema_file: prediction_event.avsc
            auth:  # a user name and a password
              - ${REGISTRY_USER}
              - ${REGISTRY_PASSWORD}
            verify: ${REGISTRY_CA_FILE}  # true, false or a CA file or directory
            cert:  # a client certificate file and its key file
              - ${REGISTRY_CERT_FILE}
              - ${REGISTRY_KEY_FILE}
            headers: {X-Team: shop}  # added to every request
            proxy: http://proxy.example.com:3128
            timeout: 30  # seconds for each step of a request
            max_retries: 5

import os
import ssl

from avro_and_pydantic_models import PredictionRecord

from desflow import KafkaEgress
from desflow.connectors.egress.kafka import ConfluentAvroSerializer


def registry_egress() -> KafkaEgress:
    """The egress of the Avro shop, with a serializer for a secured registry."""
    serializer = ConfluentAvroSerializer(
        registry_url=os.environ["SCHEMA_REGISTRY_URL"],
        schema_str=PredictionRecord.avro_schema(),
        auth=(os.environ["REGISTRY_USER"], os.environ["REGISTRY_PASSWORD"]),
        # True, False, a CA file or directory, or an ssl.SSLContext
        verify=ssl.create_default_context(cafile=os.environ["REGISTRY_CA_FILE"]),
        # A client certificate file and its key file
        cert=(os.environ["REGISTRY_CERT_FILE"], os.environ["REGISTRY_KEY_FILE"]),
        headers={"X-Team": "shop"},  # added to every request
        proxy="http://proxy.example.com:3128",
        timeout=30,  # seconds for each step of a request
        max_retries=5,
    )
    return KafkaEgress(
        bootstrap_servers=os.environ["KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS"],
        topics={"ml-predictions": {"serializer": serializer}},
    )

A request to the registry that times out is retried up to max_retries times with a short random wait. With the defaults, timeout: 10 and max_retries: 3, a request takes up to about 50 seconds for each registry URL. A larger timeout or max_retries makes it longer, and timeout: null sets no limit. The Kafka sink and the Kafka source wait for the registry in a worker thread, so the other sinks and sources of the run go on. When the registry fails for a time (a 5xx answer, a timeout or a lost connection) or throttles the call (a 408 or 429 answer, or the Glue error ThrottlingException), the Kafka sink keeps the batch and encodes it again after a wait that grows to one minute, with its connection to Kafka open. When the registry refuses the credentials or the access (a 401 or 403 answer, or the Glue error AccessDeniedException, or a Glue client that finds no credentials), it would refuse every record, so the Kafka sink or the Kafka source stops. The run logs a line at ERROR that starts with Egress KafkaEgress stopped: or Ingress KafkaIngress stopped: and gives the registry's error. When the registry refuses one record (any other 4xx answer, or a value the schema cannot encode), the sink skips that record with a warning that names its key and sends the rest of the batch. The Kafka source logs the error and skips that message, and the next message asks the registry again. The simulation goes on while each sink's queue has room. Once a queue stays full, the run stops with an error, as Egress describes.

The JSON Schema and Protobuf serializers of Use Schema Serializers take the same arguments. The AWS Glue serializers do not: they take registry_name and boto3.

docs.title: Check the Result
docs.text:
Set KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS, KAFKA_API_KEY and KAFKA_API_SECRET, then run desflow run kafka_security.yaml, python kafka_security.py or python kafka_security_low_level.py. Each runs for one simulated minute, ends at once and publishes the same events to sim-events.

The mTLS and MSK steps run the same shop. Run desflow run kafka_security_mtls.yaml or desflow run kafka_security_msk.yaml, or set KAFKA_CONNECTION=mtls or KAFKA_CONNECTION=msk (with the variables of the mTLS step, KAFKA_CA_FILE, KAFKA_CERT_FILE and KAFKA_KEY_FILE) before python kafka_security.py or python kafka_security_low_level.py. The secured registry runs with desflow run kafka_security_registry.yaml, python kafka_security_registry.py or python kafka_security_registry_low_level.py.

The Kafka ingress and KafkaAdminConnector take the same security settings in their config: see Ingress.

"""The secured Kafka connections of the Connect to Secure Kafka page.

The Builder and Low-level forms of the shop import their egress from this file:
kafka_security.py (builder) and kafka_security_low_level.py use it directly, and the YAML
files set the same keys in the `config` of their sink. It builds no simulation. Each
function builds the egress of one kind of cluster, and `selected_egress()` picks one by the
variable KAFKA_CONNECTION: sasl (the default), mtls or msk. The SASL egress reads
KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS, KAFKA_API_KEY and KAFKA_API_SECRET, the mTLS egress reads
KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS, KAFKA_CA_FILE, KAFKA_CERT_FILE and KAFKA_KEY_FILE, and the MSK
egress calls AWS when the sink starts.

`registry_egress()` needs avro_and_pydantic_models.py of Use Avro and Pydantic beside this
file, and the registry variables of kafka_security_registry.yaml.

After a shop has run with the SASL egress, `python kafka_security_connections.py` prints
the first events of sim-events.
"""

# Each section carries its own imports, as the page shows it.
# ruff: noqa: E402, F811

import os
from typing import Any, Dict

from desflow import KafkaEgress


def sasl_connection() -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """The settings of a cluster that uses SASL. The environment holds the credentials."""
    return dict(
        bootstrap_servers=os.environ["KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS"],
        # Passed as they are to the Kafka client
        security_protocol="SASL_SSL",
        sasl_mechanism="PLAIN",  # or SCRAM-SHA-512
        sasl_plain_username=os.environ["KAFKA_API_KEY"],
        sasl_plain_password=os.environ["KAFKA_API_SECRET"],
    )


def sasl_egress() -> KafkaEgress:
    """The egress of a cluster that uses SASL."""
    return KafkaEgress(**sasl_connection())


import os


def mtls_egress() -> KafkaEgress:
    """The egress of a cluster that requires mutual TLS."""
    return KafkaEgress(
        bootstrap_servers=os.environ["KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS"],
        security_protocol="SSL",
        # The arguments of aiokafka.helpers.create_ssl_context
        ssl={
            "cafile": os.environ["KAFKA_CA_FILE"],
            "certfile": os.environ["KAFKA_CERT_FILE"],
            "keyfile": os.environ["KAFKA_KEY_FILE"],
        },
    )


def msk_egress() -> KafkaEgress:
    """The egress of an Amazon MSK cluster with IAM access control."""
    return KafkaEgress(
        bootstrap_servers="b-1.my-msk.amazonaws.com:9098",
        security_protocol="SASL_SSL",
        sasl_mechanism="OAUTHBEARER",
        # The token comes from the AWS credentials of your environment or role
        sasl_oauth_token_provider={"type": "aws_msk_iam", "region": "us-east-1"},
    )


import os
import ssl

from avro_and_pydantic_models import PredictionRecord

from desflow import KafkaEgress
from desflow.connectors.egress.kafka import ConfluentAvroSerializer


def registry_egress() -> KafkaEgress:
    """The egress of the Avro shop, with a serializer for a secured registry."""
    serializer = ConfluentAvroSerializer(
        registry_url=os.environ["SCHEMA_REGISTRY_URL"],
        schema_str=PredictionRecord.avro_schema(),
        auth=(os.environ["REGISTRY_USER"], os.environ["REGISTRY_PASSWORD"]),
        # True, False, a CA file or directory, or an ssl.SSLContext
        verify=ssl.create_default_context(cafile=os.environ["REGISTRY_CA_FILE"]),
        # A client certificate file and its key file
        cert=(os.environ["REGISTRY_CERT_FILE"], os.environ["REGISTRY_KEY_FILE"]),
        headers={"X-Team": "shop"},  # added to every request
        proxy="http://proxy.example.com:3128",
        timeout=30,  # seconds for each step of a request
        max_retries=5,
    )
    return KafkaEgress(
        bootstrap_servers=os.environ["KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS"],
        topics={"ml-predictions": {"serializer": serializer}},
    )


import os


def selected_egress() -> KafkaEgress:
    """The egress that KAFKA_CONNECTION names: sasl (the default), mtls or msk."""
    makers = {"sasl": sasl_egress, "mtls": mtls_egress, "msk": msk_egress}
    return makers[os.environ.get("KAFKA_CONNECTION", "sasl")]()


import asyncio

from aiokafka import AIOKafkaConsumer


async def show_events(count: int = 3) -> None:
    """Prints the first events of sim-events, read with the settings of the SASL egress."""
    consumer = AIOKafkaConsumer(
        "sim-events", **sasl_connection(), auto_offset_reset="earliest"
    )
    await consumer.start()
    try:
        for _ in range(count):
            message = await asyncio.wait_for(consumer.getone(), timeout=10)
            print(message.value.decode())
    finally:
        await consumer.stop()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(show_events())

"""The shop of the Connect to Secure Kafka page, built with the builder API.

`build(egress)` gives the shop with the egress it is given. Run `python kafka_security.py`
to publish to a cluster that uses SASL PLAIN, such as Confluent Cloud: set
KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS, KAFKA_API_KEY and KAFKA_API_SECRET. Set KAFKA_CONNECTION to mtls
or msk to publish to a cluster of that kind instead, as kafka_security_connections.py sets
out. That file, which holds the egresses, must be beside this one.
"""

# ruff: noqa: E402

import logging

from kafka_security_connections import (
    msk_egress,
    mtls_egress,
    sasl_egress,
    selected_egress,
)

from desflow import KafkaEgress, SimulationContext


def build(egress: KafkaEgress) -> SimulationContext:
    """Builds the shop, with `egress` as its one sink."""
    app = (
        SimulationContext(sim_id="Shop", factor=0, random_seed=42)
        .add_resource("packers", current_cap=1, max_cap=1)
        .add_service("packing", dist="constant", value=1.5)
        .add_arrival("orders", dist="exponential", rate=0.5)
        .add_egress(egress)
    )

    @app.task(service_id="packing", resource_id="packers")
    def pack_order(task_id: int):
        return {"event_type": "order_packed"}

    @app.arrival_loop("orders")
    def orders(context: SimulationContext):
        while True:
            order = yield context.wait_for_arrival("orders")
            context.spawn(pack_order(context.next_instance("pack_order"), entity=order))

    return app


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(
        level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s [%(asctime)s] %(message)s"
    )
    build(selected_egress()).run(until="1 min")


def sasl_app() -> SimulationContext:
    """The shop with the egress of a cluster that uses SASL."""
    return build(sasl_egress())


def mtls_app() -> SimulationContext:
    """The shop with the egress of a cluster that requires mutual TLS."""
    return build(mtls_egress())


def msk_app() -> SimulationContext:
    """The shop with the egress of an Amazon MSK cluster."""
    return build(msk_egress())

"""The Connect to Secure Kafka guide, low-level API: a shop that publishes its events
through the egress of kafka_security_connections.py, which must be beside this script.

Set KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS, KAFKA_API_KEY and KAFKA_API_SECRET, then run
`python kafka_security_low_level.py`. It runs for one minute and publishes to a cluster
that uses SASL. Set KAFKA_CONNECTION to mtls or msk to publish to a cluster of that kind
instead, as kafka_security_connections.py sets out.
"""

import itertools
import logging

from kafka_security_connections import msk_egress, mtls_egress, selected_egress

from desflow import (
    CapacityConfig,
    DistributionConfig,
    DynamicRealtimeEnvironment,
    DynamicResource,
    Sampler,
    SimParameter,
)

PARAMS = SimParameter(
    sim_id="Shop",
    arrival={"orders": DistributionConfig(dist="exponential", rate=0.5)},
    service={"packing": DistributionConfig(dist="constant", value=1.5)},
    resources={"packers": CapacityConfig(current_cap=1, max_cap=1)},
)


def pack_order(env, packers, sampler, key, task_id):
    path_id = "Shop.service.packing"
    env.publish_event(
        key,
        {
            "path_id": path_id,
            "sim_id": "Shop",
            "service": "packing",
            "status": "queued",
        },
        "pack_order",
        task_id,
    )
    with packers.request() as unit:
        yield unit
        env.publish_event(
            key,
            {
                "path_id": path_id,
                "sim_id": "Shop",
                "service": "packing",
                "status": "started",
            },
            "pack_order",
            task_id,
        )
        yield env.timeout(sampler.sample(env.registry.get_config(path_id)))
        env.publish_event(key, {"event_type": "order_packed"}, "pack_order", task_id)


def orders(env, packers, sampler):
    gap = env.registry.get_config("Shop.arrival.orders")
    for number in itertools.count(1):
        yield env.timeout(sampler.sample(gap))
        env.process(pack_order(env, packers, sampler, f"orders-{number}", number - 1))


def shop(sinks: list, factor: float = 0.0) -> DynamicRealtimeEnvironment:
    """The shop, publishing to the sinks given."""
    env = DynamicRealtimeEnvironment(factor=factor)
    env.registry.register_sim_parameter(PARAMS)
    env.setup_egress(sinks)
    packers = DynamicResource(env, "Shop", "packers")
    env.process(orders(env, packers, Sampler(seed=42)))
    return env


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(
        level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s [%(asctime)s] %(message)s"
    )
    env = shop([selected_egress()])  # KAFKA_CONNECTION picks the cluster
    try:
        env.run(until=60)
    finally:
        env.teardown()


def mtls_shop() -> DynamicRealtimeEnvironment:
    """The shop with the egress of a cluster that requires mutual TLS."""
    return shop([mtls_egress()])


def msk_shop() -> DynamicRealtimeEnvironment:
    """The shop with the egress of an Amazon MSK cluster."""
    return shop([msk_egress()])

docs.title: Write a Connector
docs.text: Write a connector of your own when a model must read changes from, or write records to, a system that desflow has no connector for. This page writes an egress that writes each event as a row of a CSV file, and an ingress that follows a JSON Lines file of changes. Neither needs a service.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text: • Ingress and Egress describe the connectors desflow has and the threads they run on.

docs.title: Write an Egress
docs.text:
An egress subclasses BaseEgress and has one method, async run(queue). desflow runs it on the egress thread's asyncio loop, apart from the simulation. The queue holds batches: each batch is a list of records, in the record shape every sink receives. run takes a batch with get_nowait, and sleeps when the queue is empty so the other connectors on the loop can run:

docs/snippets/yaml/write_a_connector_logic.py:egress
class CsvEgress(BaseEgress):
    """Writes one CSV row per record it is given: its time, key and task, then the
    payload fields that `columns` names. The sink's `when` keeps telemetry out."""

    def __init__(self, path: str, columns: List[str]):
        self.path = Path(path)
        self.columns = list(columns)
        self.active_tasks = 0  # teardown waits while a write is in progress

    async def run(self, egress_queue: queue.Queue) -> None:
        with self.path.open("w", newline="") as file:
            writer = csv.writer(file)
            writer.writerow(["sim_ts", "key", "task", *self.columns])
            while True:
                try:
                    batch = egress_queue.get_nowait()
                except queue.Empty:
                    await asyncio.sleep(0.1)  # let the other connectors run
                    continue
                self.active_tasks += 1
                try:
                    rows = [self._row(record) for record in batch]
                    # A file write blocks, so it runs on a worker thread
                    await asyncio.to_thread(self._write, file, writer, rows)
                finally:
                    self.active_tasks -= 1

    def _row(self, record: dict) -> list:
        value = record["value"] if isinstance(record.get("value"), dict) else {}
        fields = [value.get(column) for column in self.columns]
        return [record["sim_ts"], record.get("key"), record.get("task"), *fields]

    @staticmethod
    def _write(file, writer, rows: list) -> None:
        writer.writerows(rows)
        file.flush()

Three rules apply to every egress:

  • Do not block the loop. A write that blocks, such as a file write or a client without async, runs on a worker thread with asyncio.to_thread.
  • Count the writes in progress. At the end of the run, teardown waits for every queue to empty, then waits while the sink's active_tasks is above 0. A batch taken from the queue but not yet written is therefore not lost.
  • Copy before you change a record. Every sink receives the same dictionaries, so a sink that changes one in place changes what the others write. This sink builds new rows.

An error that ends run is logged at ERROR with the connector's name. The sink then takes no more batches, so once its queue is full the simulation waits, and after drain_stall_seconds the run raises RuntimeError, as Egress describes.

docs.title: Write an Ingress
docs.text:
An ingress subclasses BaseIngress and has one method too, async run(queue), which desflow runs on the ingress thread. It puts each change on the queue as a (path, value) pair. parse_change turns a message such as {"path": "Shop.resources.packers.current_cap", "value": 2} into that pair, with the check the built-in connectors use. The ingress monitor applies what is queued every 0.1 simulation seconds, and the registry checks each value before it stores it (Live Parameters):

docs/snippets/yaml/write_a_connector_logic.py:ingress
class JsonlIngress(BaseIngress):
    """Follows a JSON Lines file and applies each line it adds, such as
    `{"path": "Shop.resources.packers.current_cap", "value": 2}`."""

    def __init__(self, path: str, poll: float = 0.1):
        self.path = Path(path)
        self.poll = poll

    async def run(self, ingress_queue: queue.Queue) -> None:
        read = 0  # the lines already applied
        while True:
            if self.path.exists():
                # A file read blocks, so it runs on a worker thread
                text = await asyncio.to_thread(self.path.read_text)
                # Only whole lines: a writer may be partway through the last one
                lines = text[: text.rfind("\n") + 1].splitlines()
                for line in lines[read:]:
                    try:
                        ingress_queue.put(parse_change(json.loads(line)))
                    except ValueError as error:  # also a line that is not JSON
                        logger.warning("Skipped a line of %s: %s", self.path, error)
                read = len(lines)
            await asyncio.sleep(self.poll)

A line of the file that is not a change is logged as one WARNING and skipped, as the built-in connectors do, so one bad message does not stop the run. At the end of the run desflow cancels run, so it needs no way to stop.

docs.title: Use Them
docs.text:
A connector of your own goes where a built-in one goes. Each config key is an argument of the class's constructor. An egress receives every event and telemetry record, and when limits it, as Egress shows. This sink takes events only.

YAMLBuilderLow-level docs/snippets/yaml/write_a_connector.yaml:connectors
ingress:
  - type: !python write_a_connector_logic.JsonlIngress
    config: {path: changes.jsonl}

egress:
  - type: !python write_a_connector_logic.CsvEgress
    when: events  # events only; the readings of telemetry stay out of the file
    config: {path: events.csv, columns: [status, event_type]}

The classes are in write_a_connector_logic.py, beside the blueprint. type: !python names the class, and the loader builds it with config as its arguments.

docs/snippets/guides/write_a_connector.py:builder
app = (
    SimulationContext(sim_id="Shop", factor=0.05, random_seed=42)
    .add_resource("packers", current_cap=1, max_cap=3)
    .add_service("packing", dist="constant", value=1.5)
    .add_arrival("orders", dist="constant", value=1.0)
    .add_ingress(JsonlIngress("changes.jsonl"))
    .add_egress(
        CsvEgress("events.csv", columns=["status", "event_type"]),
        when=lambda record: record["stream_type"] == "event",  # no telemetry
    )
)

@app.task(service_id="packing", resource_id="packers")
def pack_order(task_id: int):
    return {"event_type": "order_packed"}

@app.arrival_loop("orders")
def order_generator(context: SimulationContext):
    while True:
        order = yield context.wait_for_arrival("orders")
        context.spawn(pack_order(context.next_instance("pack_order"), entity=order))

app.run(until=20)

env = DynamicRealtimeEnvironment(factor=0.05)
env.registry.register_sim_parameter(
    SimParameter(
        sim_id="Shop",
        service={"packing": DistributionConfig(dist="constant", value=1.5)},
        resources={"packers": CapacityConfig(current_cap=1, max_cap=3)},
    )
)
env.setup_ingress([JsonlIngress("changes.jsonl")])

    [CsvEgress("events.csv", columns=["status", "event_type"])],
    predicates=[lambda record: record["stream_type"] == "event"],  # no telemetry
)
packers = DynamicResource(env, "Shop", "packers")

def order(env, number):
    key, path_id = f"orders-{number}", "Shop.service.packing"
    env.publish_event(
        key,
        {
            "path_id": path_id,
            "sim_id": "Shop",
            "service": "packing",
            "status": "queued",
        },
        "pack_order",
        number - 1,
    )
    with packers.request() as request:
        yield request
        env.publish_event(
            key,
            {
                "path_id": path_id,
                "sim_id": "Shop",
                "service": "packing",
                "status": "started",
            },
            "pack_order",
            number - 1,
        )
        yield env.timeout(1.5)
    env.publish_event(key, {"event_type": "order_packed"}, "pack_order", number - 1)

def arrivals(env):
    number = 0
    while True:
        yield env.timeout(1.0)
        number += 1
        env.process(order(env, number))

env.process(arrivals(env))
try:
    env.run(until=20)
finally:
    env.teardown()  # writes what is still buffered and stops the threads

The low-level API attaches the same objects with setup_ingress and setup_egress, and teardown waits for the CSV sink to write what is still queued.

The shop is paced at factor: 0.05, so 20 simulation seconds pass in each real second, and the run lasts one second of real time. An ingress reads its source while time passes, and a run at factor: 0 can end before the source is read once.

docs.title: Check the Result
docs.text:
Before the run, changes.jsonl holds one line, which sets the packers to 2 units. An order arrives every second from 1 second, and each takes 1.5 seconds, so one packer would fall behind. The ingress applies the change in the first moments of the run, and from then on each order starts when it arrives. The first rows of events.csv:

sim_ts,key,task,status,event_type
1.0,orders-1,pack_order,queued,
1.0,orders-1,pack_order,started,
2.0,orders-2,pack_order,queued,
2.0,orders-2,pack_order,started,
2.5,orders-1,pack_order,,order_packed

orders-2 starts at 2 seconds while orders-1 is still being packed, so the second unit is there. By 20 seconds, 19 orders have arrived and started, and the 18 that arrived by 18 seconds are packed. That is 19 queued, 19 started and 18 order_packed events: 56 rows. All three forms write the same rows.

Save the files that the tab of your form names from Full Files in one folder, each under the last part of its title, and run the command of your form from that folder:

YAMLBuilderLow-level

Save write_a_connector.yaml and write_a_connector_logic.py. The first line writes the change that the ingress reads. The blueprint does not write it:

echo '{"path": "Shop.resources.packers.current_cap", "value": 2}' > changes.jsonl
desflow run write_a_connector.yaml
head -n 6 events.csv
wc -l events.csv

sim_ts,key,task,status,event_type
1.0,orders-1,pack_order,queued,
1.0,orders-1,pack_order,started,
2.0,orders-2,pack_order,queued,
2.0,orders-2,pack_order,started,
2.5,orders-1,pack_order,,order_packed
      57 events.csv

The 57 lines are the header and the 56 rows. The spaces before the count depend on your system.

Save write_a_connector.py, write_a_connector_logic.py and the blueprint write_a_connector.yaml, because the script runs the YAML form first. python write_a_connector.py writes changes.jsonl, runs the YAML form and then the builder form, and prints the packers' units at the end and the number of rows in events.csv for each:

yaml_form       packers: 2, rows in events.csv: 56
builder_form    packers: 2, rows in events.csv: 56

Save write_a_connector_low_level.py and write_a_connector_logic.py. python write_a_connector_low_level.py does the same for the low-level form:

low_level_form  packers: 2, rows in events.csv: 56

Every form uses the two connectors in write_a_connector_logic.py unchanged. Put it, the blueprint and the scripts in one folder, and run the scripts from there.

Full files docs/snippets/yaml/write_a_connector_logic.py
"""Python for write_a_connector.yaml: an egress that writes events to a CSV file and
an ingress that follows a JSON Lines file of changes, as the Write a Connector guide
builds them."""

import asyncio
import csv
import json
import logging
import queue
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List

from desflow.connectors.egress.base import BaseEgress
from desflow.connectors.ingress.base import BaseIngress, parse_change

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class CsvEgress(BaseEgress):
    """Writes one CSV row per record it is given: its time, key and task, then the
    payload fields that `columns` names. The sink's `when` keeps telemetry out."""

    def __init__(self, path: str, columns: List[str]):
        self.path = Path(path)
        self.columns = list(columns)
        self.active_tasks = 0  # teardown waits while a write is in progress

    async def run(self, egress_queue: queue.Queue) -> None:
        with self.path.open("w", newline="") as file:
            writer = csv.writer(file)
            writer.writerow(["sim_ts", "key", "task", *self.columns])
            while True:
                try:
                    batch = egress_queue.get_nowait()
                except queue.Empty:
                    await asyncio.sleep(0.1)  # let the other connectors run
                    continue
                self.active_tasks += 1
                try:
                    rows = [self._row(record) for record in batch]
                    # A file write blocks, so it runs on a worker thread
                    await asyncio.to_thread(self._write, file, writer, rows)
                finally:
                    self.active_tasks -= 1

    def _row(self, record: dict) -> list:
        value = record["value"] if isinstance(record.get("value"), dict) else {}
        fields = [value.get(column) for column in self.columns]
        return [record["sim_ts"], record.get("key"), record.get("task"), *fields]

    @staticmethod
    def _write(file, writer, rows: list) -> None:
        writer.writerows(rows)
        file.flush()


class JsonlIngress(BaseIngress):
    """Follows a JSON Lines file and applies each line it adds, such as
    `{"path": "Shop.resources.packers.current_cap", "value": 2}`."""

    def __init__(self, path: str, poll: float = 0.1):
        self.path = Path(path)
        self.poll = poll

    async def run(self, ingress_queue: queue.Queue) -> None:
        read = 0  # the lines already applied
        while True:
            if self.path.exists():
                # A file read blocks, so it runs on a worker thread
                text = await asyncio.to_thread(self.path.read_text)
                # Only whole lines: a writer may be partway through the last one
                lines = text[: text.rfind("\n") + 1].splitlines()
                for line in lines[read:]:
                    try:
                        ingress_queue.put(parse_change(json.loads(line)))
                    except ValueError as error:  # also a line that is not JSON
                        logger.warning("Skipped a line of %s: %s", self.path, error)
                read = len(lines)
            await asyncio.sleep(self.poll)
