Checked by 12 tests in c1_timed_wait (5), builder_additions (2), yaml_only (4) and c2_wait_for_one_or_all (1).

An event that happens after a delay and carries a value. Explained in Timeout value.

  • SimPy: Timeout(delay, value)
  • YAML: wait: {timeout: {after: 40 s, value: ...}}
  • Builder: the same mapping in wait=
  • Low-level: env.timeout(delay, value)

Checked by 2 tests in c1_events (1) and yaml_only (1).

docs.title: Processes
docs.text:
Starts a process and suspends the one that started it until the new process ends. Explained in Start and wait for a process.

  • SimPy: Start a process and wait for it
  • YAML: wait: {task: inspect}
  • Builder: wait={"task": "inspect"}, or yield context.call("inspect")
  • Low-level: yield env.process(child())

Checked by 13 tests in c1_process_interaction (5), yaml_only (7) and generator_streams (1).

Gives the waiting process the value a process returns when it ends. Explained in Process return value.

  • SimPy: A process's return value
  • YAML: wait.inspect.value.<field>, the last payload of the child flow
  • Builder: the same, or the value of context.call(...)
  • Low-level: value = yield env.process(child())

Checked by 1 test in c1_process_interaction.

Raises an exception from a process in the process that waits for it. Explained in Process failure.

  • SimPy: An exception in a process reaches the process that waits for it
  • YAML: fail, fail_reason and on_fail on a task, and on_fail alone for a failed wait or step; a failure no on_fail handles fails the waiting task
  • Builder: the same, and a function that raises fails its task
  • Low-level: try: yield env.process(child()) and except
  • Where desflow differs: By default (on_unhandled_failure is stop) a failure no task waits for stops the run, matching SimPy and the low-level API, where an exception nobody handles stops the run; under on_unhandled_failure of continue it ends the entity's flow in YAML and the builder, publishes failed and is counted, and the run goes on.

Checked by 4 tests in c1_process_interaction (2), builder_additions (1) and yaml_only (1).

Tells whether a process is still running. Explained in Process inspection.

  • SimPy: Process.is_alive
  • YAML: wait.<branch>.done, .ok and .value after the wait
  • Builder: the process context.spawn and context.call return
  • Low-level: the process env.process returns

Checked by 2 tests in c1_process_interaction.

Gives the event a process waits for at this moment. Explained in The running process.

  • SimPy: Process.target
  • YAML: process.name, process.instance, process.target in a condition
  • Builder: context.env.active_process; .name and .target on a process
  • Low-level: env.active_process.name, .target

Checked by 7 tests in c1_process_interaction (5), c2_wait_for_one_or_all (1) and yaml_only (1).

Gives the name of the function that started a process. Explained in The running process.

  • SimPy: Process.name
  • YAML: process.name, process.instance, process.target in a condition
  • Builder: context.env.active_process; .name and .target on a process
  • Low-level: env.active_process.name, .target

Checked by 7 tests in c1_process_interaction (5), c2_wait_for_one_or_all (1) and yaml_only (1).

Suspends a process until another process, started earlier, ends. Explained in Wait for a process already running.

  • SimPy: Wait for a process that is already running
  • YAML: wait: {running: {task: charge, where: ...}}
  • Builder: the same in wait=, or yield a process from context.spawn or call
  • Low-level: yield process

Checked by 8 tests in c1_processes (7) and yaml_only (1).

Starts a process after a delay instead of now. Explained in Start a process after a delay.

  • SimPy: start_delayed(env, generator, delay)
  • YAML: spawn: {task: courier, after: 3 s}
  • Builder: spawn={"task", "after"}, or context.spawn(generator, delay=3)
  • Low-level: simpy.util.start_delayed(env, generator, 3)

Checked by 3 tests in c1_processes.

docs.title: Conditions
docs.text:
An event that happens when the first of several events happens. Explained in Wait for one event.

  • SimPy: AnyOf and env.any_of
  • YAML: wait: {any: {stock: {signal: restocked}, limit: {timeout: 3}}}
  • Builder: wait={"any": {...}}
  • Low-level: yield a | b
  • Where desflow differs: Losing signal, timeout and condition branches are dropped when the wait ends; losing child flows keep running, as SimPy leaves processes running. A request branch not yet granted when the wait ends is cancelled; a SimPy with block held over the rest of the task leaves it queued.

Checked by 8 tests in c2_wait_for_one_or_all (2) and yaml_only (6).

An event that happens when all of several events have happened. Explained in Wait for all events.

  • SimPy: AllOf and env.all_of
  • YAML: wait: {all: {...}}
  • Builder: wait={"all": {...}}
  • Low-level: yield a & b

Checked by 9 tests in c2_wait_for_one_or_all (2) and yaml_only (7).

Gives the events of a condition that have happened, with their values, in the order of the condition. Explained in Wait for one event.

  • SimPy: ConditionValue
  • YAML: wait: {any: {stock: {signal: restocked}, limit: {timeout: 3}}}
  • Builder: wait={"any": {...}}
  • Low-level: yield a | b
  • Where desflow differs: Losing signal, timeout and condition branches are dropped when the wait ends; losing child flows keep running, as SimPy leaves processes running. A request branch not yet granted when the wait ends is cancelled; a SimPy with block held over the rest of the task leaves it queued.

Checked by 8 tests in c2_wait_for_one_or_all (2) and yaml_only (6).

Fails a condition at once when one of its events fails. Explained in Wait for all events.

  • SimPy: A member that fails fails the condition
  • YAML: wait: {all: {...}}
  • Builder: wait={"all": {...}}
  • Low-level: yield a & b

Checked by 9 tests in c2_wait_for_one_or_all (2) and yaml_only (7).

Builds a condition from other conditions, such as (a & b) | c. Explained in Nested and mixed conditions.

  • SimPy: Nested and mixed conditions
  • YAML: wait: {all: {look: {task: inspect}, either: {any: {...}}}}
  • Builder: wait={"all": {...}} with nested groups
  • Low-level: yield (a | b) & c

Checked by 3 tests in c2_conditions.

Builds a condition with a rule of your own that decides when it happens. Explained in A condition with a custom rule.

  • SimPy: Condition(env, evaluate, events) with a rule of your own
  • YAML: wait: {at_least: 2, of: {...}}
  • Builder: wait={"at_least": 2, "of": {...}}
  • Low-level: Condition(env, lambda evs, c: c >= 2, [...])

Checked by 6 tests in c2_conditions (4) and yaml_only (2).

Builds a condition from an empty list of events, which happens at once. Explained in A condition over no events.

  • SimPy: A condition over no events
  • YAML: wait: {any: {}} or wait: {all: {}}
  • Builder: wait={"any": {}}
  • Low-level: env.any_of([])

Checked by 1 test in c2_wait_for_one_or_all.

Uses a request, get or put as one of the events of a condition. Explained in Request, put or get as a wait branch.

  • SimPy: A request, get or put as a member of a condition
  • YAML: wait: {request: packers}, wait: {get: {store: parcels}}, wait: {put: {store: ...}}
  • Builder: wait={"request": "packers"} or wait={"get": {...}}
  • Low-level: yield req | env.timeout(3)

Checked by 11 tests in c2_conditions (10) and c2_wait_for_one_or_all (1).

docs.title: Interrupts
docs.text:
Raises an Interrupt in a process that is waiting, with a cause. Explained in Interrupt while waiting.

  • SimPy: Process.interrupt(cause) while the process waits
  • YAML: interrupt: {task: waiter} on a scenario step or a task; on_interrupt on the task
  • Builder: context.interrupt("waiter"); @app.task(on_interrupt=...)
  • Low-level: process.interrupt(cause), caught as simpy.Interrupt
  • Where desflow differs: A task's own spawn: and interrupt: keys run in a fixed order, interrupt first, so one task cannot interrupt the instance it spawns with them. List a spawn and then an interrupt in on:, which run in the order written, or use context.spawn and context.interrupt.

Checked by 5 tests in c3_interrupts (3) and yaml_only (2).

Interrupts a process during a delay, which ends the delay early. Explained in Interrupt during service.

  • SimPy: An interrupt during a timeout
  • YAML: on_interrupt: resume, restart or abandon, and on_interrupt_run for a task that runs first
  • Builder: @app.task(on_interrupt=...)
  • Low-level: except simpy.Interrupt, then request again

Checked by 27 tests in c3_interrupts (14), c1_process_interaction (1) and yaml_only (12).

The exception an interrupted process receives, and the cause given with it. Explained in Interrupt during service.

  • SimPy: Interrupt and Interrupt.cause

Grants one waiting get for each put made at the same time. Explained in Equal-time puts and gets.

With filtered and unfiltered gets in one queue, gets at the same instant can therefore resume in a different order than in FilterStore; each get receives the same item.

docs.title: Where desflow Differs
docs.text:
Holds the functions that run when an event is processed. In Events and Timeout.

  • SimPy: Event.callbacks
  • Gap M2: A Builder on= refuses a callable. A generator started with add_process can add a function to an event's callbacks.

Refuses a capacity of 0 or below for a resource, container or store. In Resources.

  • SimPy: Capacity must be above 0
  • Difference kept by design: A resource, store or container may have a capacity of 0, at the start or later, because its capacity changes during a run: a shift with no packers, a shelf that is closed. At capacity 0 a resource grants no request, and a store or container accepts no put, until the capacity rises; a get still takes what a store or container holds.

docs.title: SimPy Examples
docs.text:
SimPy's documentation ships seven example programs. Each page here takes one of them, shows SimPy's code piece by piece, and shows the same piece written in desflow as a YAML blueprint, with the builder API, and with the low-level API. Every desflow version is a file that desflow examples get downloads and a test runs.

Example What it shows Bank Renege customers who wait too long at a counter go away Carwash a car keeps a washing machine while the wash runs Machine Shop machines break down, and a repair preempts the repairman's other jobs Movie Renege a film that sells out sends its queue away Gas Station Refueling cars drain a tank that a tank truck refills Process Communication messages through a store, one to one and broadcast Event Latency each message reaches the receiver after a fixed delay

docs.title: How to Read the Pages
docs.text:
Each page keeps the system of SimPy's example and changes three things that a reader would otherwise take for a difference in the model.

  • Times are seconds. SimPy's times have no unit. desflow reads each time unit as one second. In Carwash, Machine Shop and Movie Renege, SimPy counts minutes, and each of its minutes is one second here. A run of 20 minutes in SimPy is a run of 20 seconds in desflow.
  • Numbers differ from SimPy's output. desflow draws each random value from its own stream, named by the place where the value is used, such as tasks.customer.patience. A seed of 42 gives different numbers from SimPy's random.seed(42). Each page shows SimPy's output beside the figures of the desflow run. The two have the same structure and different numbers.
  • Machine Shop writes breakdowns as tasks. SimPy interrupts the process that makes parts. The repair is then a request for the repairman, who also does other jobs. The page writes each machine's failures as a task that interrupts the machine's part task, so that the repair is an ordinary request at priority 1.

SimPy's code is shown with its licence notice. Coming from SimPy maps each SimPy construct to its desflow form, and SimPy Compatibility lists what is supported.

docs.title: Bank Renege
docs.text: One counter serves five customers, and a customer who waits longer than their patience goes away. This is SimPy's Bank Renege example, written in desflow.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
SimPy's example has one counter and 5 customers. The first customer arrives at time 0 and the others at exponential gaps with a mean of 10. Each customer has a patience drawn between 1 and 3, and goes away (reneges) if the counter is not free by then. A customer who reaches the counter is served for an exponential time with a mean of 12. SimPy counts no unit, and desflow reads each unit as one second.

The example needs only desflow, which each Quick Start in Run It installs, and no other service. desflow examples get simpy-bank-renege --api yaml downloads it, as Get an Example shows. SimPy Examples says how these pages read SimPy's times and numbers. SimPy's own page for the example is on its documentation site.

docs.title: Customers Arrive
docs.text:
SimPy's source starts a customer at time 0 and then one after each gap.

def source(env, number, interval, counter):

docs.title: Customer Waits or Reneges
docs.text:
SimPy's customer requests the counter and waits for either the counter or its patience, whichever comes first.

docs/snippets/simpy/bank_renege.py:customer-waits-or-reneges
def customer(env, name, counter, time_in_bank):
    """Customer arrives, is served and leaves."""
    arrive = env.now
    print(f'{arrive:7.4f} {name}: Here I am')

    with counter.request() as req:
        patience = random.uniform(MIN_PATIENCE, MAX_PATIENCE)
        # Wait for the counter or abort at the end of our tether
        results = yield req | env.timeout(patience)

        wait = env.now - arrive

        if req in results:
            # We got to the counter
            print(f'{env.now:7.4f} {name}: Waited {wait:6.3f}')

            tib = random.expovariate(1.0 / time_in_bank)
            yield env.timeout(tib)
            print(f'{env.now:7.4f} {name}: Finished')

        else:
            # We reneged
            print(f'{env.now:7.4f} {name}: RENEGED after {wait:6.3f}')
YAMLBuilderLow-level

patience is the longest wait for the counter, drawn uniform from 1 to 3 seconds for each customer. A customer whose patience ends first publishes reneged and leaves. The service time is exponential with a mean of 12 seconds, written as the rate 1/12.

examples/yaml/simpy/bank_renege.yaml:customer-waits-or-reneges
tasks:
  customer:
    resource: counter
    patience: {gen: uniform, low: 1, high: 3}
    service_time: {gen: sample, dist: exponential, rate: 0.08333333333333333}
    payload: {event_type: finished}

The customer task takes patience and service_time as generators.

examples/builder/simpy/bank_renege_example.py:customer-waits-or-reneges
@app.task(
    name="customer",
    resource_id="counter",
    # Waits for the counter at most this long, then goes away
    patience=generator({"gen": "uniform", "low": 1, "high": 3}),
    service_time=generator(
        {"gen": "sample", "dist": "exponential", "rate": 0.08333333333333333}
    ),
)
def customer(task_id):
    """Is served at the counter."""
    return {"event_type": "finished"}

The customer function is SimPy's, with req | env.timeout(patience). It publishes reneged when req is not in the result.

examples/low-level/simpy/bank_renege_example.py:customer-waits-or-reneges
def customer(name, number):
    def publish(value):
        env.publish_event(name, value, task="customer", instance=number)

    with counter.request() as req:
        publish({"status": "queued"})
        patience = float(patiences.uniform(1, 3))
        # Waits for the counter at most `patience`, then goes away
        results = yield req | env.timeout(patience)
        if req in results:
            publish({"status": "started"})
            yield env.timeout(float(services.exponential(12.0)))
            publish({"event_type": "finished"})
        else:
            publish({"status": "reneged"})

docs.title: Check the Result
docs.text:
Two of the five customers renege: Customer03 and Customer04. Customer00 is served from time 0 and finishes at 3.536 seconds. Customer01 reaches the counter at 5.384 seconds and finishes at 10.53 seconds. Customer02 reaches the counter at 10.53 seconds and finishes at 18.266 seconds. The run has no end time, so it stops when the last customer leaves.

SimPy's own output, below, has customers who are served and customers who renege too. desflow draws each random value from its own stream, named by the place where the value is used, such as tasks.customer.patience. A seed of 42 therefore gives different numbers from SimPy's random.seed(42). The system is the same. The figures are not.

# Bank Renege: SimPy's bank_renege.py example, in YAML.
#
# The YAML version of bank_renege_example.py, which --api builder downloads. One
# counter serves five customers. The first arrives at 0 and the others about 10
# seconds apart (exponential gaps). Each customer waits for the counter for a patience
# drawn between 1 and 3 seconds, and goes away (reneged) if the counter is not free by
# then. A customer at the counter is served for about 12 seconds (exponential).
#
# SimPy's example counts seconds, as desflow does. Each value is drawn from desflow's
# random sequence for its place in the file, so the numbers differ from those SimPy
# prints.
#
# Needs no containers. Runs unpaced and ends when the last customer leaves.
# Run it from its folder with: desflow run bank_renege.yaml

simulation: {sim_id: Bank, factor: 0, random_seed: 42}

egress:
  - {type: Console}

resources:
  counter: {current_cap: 1}

arrivals:
  customers:
    dist: exponential
    rate: 0.1
    first_at: 0
    max_events: 5
    key: {gen: sequence, format: "Customer{:02d}"}
    spawn: customer

tasks:
  customer:
    resource: counter
    patience: {gen: uniform, low: 1, high: 3}
    service_time: {gen: sample, dist: exponential, rate: 0.08333333333333333}
    payload: {event_type: finished}

The script builds the model with the builder API.

examples/builder/simpy/bank_renege_example.py
"""Bank Renege: SimPy's bank_renege.py example, builder API.

One counter serves five customers. The first arrives at 0 and the others about 10
seconds apart (exponential gaps). Each customer waits for the counter for a patience
drawn between 1 and 3 seconds, and goes away (reneged) if the counter is not free by
then. A customer at the counter is served for about 12 seconds (exponential).

SimPy's example counts seconds, as desflow does. Each value is drawn from desflow's
random sequence for its place in the model, so the numbers differ from those SimPy
prints.

Needs no containers. Runs unpaced and ends when the last customer leaves.
"""

import logging

from desflow import ConsoleEgress, SimulationContext
from desflow.values import generator


def build() -> SimulationContext:
    """Builds the bank."""
    app = SimulationContext(sim_id="Bank", factor=0, random_seed=42)
    app.add_egress(ConsoleEgress())
    app.add_resource("counter", current_cap=1)
    app.add_arrival(
        "customers",
        "exponential",
        rate=0.1,
        first_at=0,
        max_events=5,
        key=lambda n: "Customer{:02d}".format(n - 1),
        spawn="customer",
    )

    @app.task(
        name="customer",
        resource_id="counter",
        # Waits for the counter at most this long, then goes away
        patience=generator({"gen": "uniform", "low": 1, "high": 3}),
        service_time=generator(
            {"gen": "sample", "dist": "exponential", "rate": 0.08333333333333333}
        ),
    )
    def customer(task_id):
        """Is served at the counter."""
        return {"event_type": "finished"}


    return app


app = build()


def run(model: SimulationContext = app) -> None:
    """Runs until the last customer leaves."""
    model.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    run()

The script wires the model by hand on DynamicRealtimeEnvironment, with SimPy's own processes.

examples/low-level/simpy/bank_renege_example.py
"""Bank Renege: SimPy's bank_renege.py example, low-level API.

The low-level version of `builder/simpy/bank_renege_example.py`: SimPy's own processes
on a `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment`. They publish with `publish_event` the records that
the YAML and builder versions publish: each customer's `queued` and `started`, its
`reneged` or `finished`, and the number of the task's instance. One counter serves
five customers. The first arrives at 0 and the others about 10 seconds apart. Each
customer waits for the counter for a patience between 1 and 3 seconds, and goes away
(reneged) if the counter is not free by then. A customer at the counter is served for
about 12 seconds.

SimPy's example counts seconds, as desflow does. Each value is drawn from desflow's
`Sampler`, from the random sequence the YAML and builder versions use for the same
place, so the three versions publish the same records.

Needs no containers. Runs unpaced and ends when the last customer leaves.
"""

import logging

import simpy

from desflow import (
    ConsoleEgress,
    DistributionConfig,
    DynamicRealtimeEnvironment,
    Sampler,
)

NEW_CUSTOMERS = 5
UNTIL = None  # the run ends when no event is left


def build(env: DynamicRealtimeEnvironment) -> None:
    """Starts the customers' source on `env`."""
    sampler = Sampler(seed=42)
    gap = DistributionConfig(dist="exponential", rate=0.1)
    gap.stream = "arrival.customers"  # the sequence the blueprint's arrival draws from
    patiences = sampler.generator("tasks.customer.patience")
    services = sampler.generator("tasks.customer.service_time")
    counter = simpy.Resource(env, capacity=1)

    def customer(name, number):
        def publish(value):
            env.publish_event(name, value, task="customer", instance=number)

        with counter.request() as req:
            publish({"status": "queued"})
            patience = float(patiences.uniform(1, 3))
            # Waits for the counter at most `patience`, then goes away
            results = yield req | env.timeout(patience)
            if req in results:
                publish({"status": "started"})
                yield env.timeout(float(services.exponential(12.0)))
                publish({"event_type": "finished"})
            else:
                publish({"status": "reneged"})


    def source():
        for i in range(NEW_CUSTOMERS):
            env.process(customer(f"Customer{i:02d}", i))
            yield env.timeout(sampler.sample(gap))

    env.process(source())


def run() -> None:
    """Runs until the last customer leaves."""
    env = DynamicRealtimeEnvironment(factor=0)
    env.setup_egress([ConsoleEgress()])
    build(env)
    try:
        env.run(until=UNTIL)
    finally:
        env.teardown()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    run()

"""
Bank renege example

Covers:

- Resources: Resource
- Condition events

Scenario:
  A counter with a random service time and customers who renege. Based on the
  program bank08.py from TheBank tutorial of SimPy 2. (KGM)

"""

import random

import simpy

RANDOM_SEED = 42
NEW_CUSTOMERS = 5  # Total number of customers
INTERVAL_CUSTOMERS = 10.0  # Generate new customers roughly every x seconds
MIN_PATIENCE = 1  # Min. customer patience
MAX_PATIENCE = 3  # Max. customer patience


def source(env, number, interval, counter):
    """Source generates customers randomly"""
    for i in range(number):
        c = customer(env, f'Customer{i:02d}', counter, time_in_bank=12.0)
        env.process(c)
        t = random.expovariate(1.0 / interval)
        yield env.timeout(t)


def customer(env, name, counter, time_in_bank):
    """Customer arrives, is served and leaves."""
    arrive = env.now
    print(f'{arrive:7.4f} {name}: Here I am')

    with counter.request() as req:
        patience = random.uniform(MIN_PATIENCE, MAX_PATIENCE)
        # Wait for the counter or abort at the end of our tether
        results = yield req | env.timeout(patience)

        wait = env.now - arrive

        if req in results:
            # We got to the counter
            print(f'{env.now:7.4f} {name}: Waited {wait:6.3f}')

            tib = random.expovariate(1.0 / time_in_bank)
            yield env.timeout(tib)
            print(f'{env.now:7.4f} {name}: Finished')

        else:
            # We reneged
            print(f'{env.now:7.4f} {name}: RENEGED after {wait:6.3f}')


# Setup and start the simulation
print('Bank renege')
random.seed(RANDOM_SEED)
env = simpy.Environment()

# Start processes and run
counter = simpy.Resource(env, capacity=1)
env.process(source(env, NEW_CUSTOMERS, INTERVAL_CUSTOMERS, counter))
env.run()

docs.title: Carwash
docs.text: Cars take a washing machine and keep it while the wash runs. This is SimPy's Carwash example, written in desflow.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
SimPy's carwash has two machines. Four cars are waiting when it opens, and then a car arrives every 5 to 9 minutes. A wash takes 5 minutes and removes 50 to 99 percent of the dirt. The run lasts 20 minutes. desflow reads each of SimPy's minutes as one second, so the run lasts 20 seconds.

The example needs only desflow, which each Quick Start in Run It installs, and no other service. desflow examples get simpy-carwash --api yaml downloads it, as Get an Example shows. SimPy Examples says how these pages read SimPy's times and numbers. SimPy's own page for the example is on its documentation site.

docs.title: Machines Wash
docs.text:
SimPy's Carwash class holds the machines and has a wash method that takes the wash time and removes dirt.

docs/snippets/simpy/carwash.py:machines-wash
class Carwash:
    """A carwash has a limited number of machines (``NUM_MACHINES``) to
    clean cars in parallel.

    Cars have to request one of the machines. When they got one, they
    can start the washing processes and wait for it to finish (which
    takes ``washtime`` minutes).

    """

    def __init__(self, env, num_machines, washtime):
        self.env = env
        self.machine = simpy.Resource(env, num_machines)
        self.washtime = washtime

    def wash(self, car):
        """The washing processes. It takes a ``car`` processes and tries
        to clean it."""
        yield self.env.timeout(self.washtime)
        pct_dirt = random.randint(50, 99)
        print(f"Carwash removed {pct_dirt}% of {car}'s dirt.")
YAMLBuilderLow-level

machine is a resource with two units, and wash is a service that takes 5 seconds. The wash task is a task of its own: it takes the service time and publishes the dirt removed, an integer from 50 to 99, in dirt_removed_pct.

resources:
  machine: {current_cap: 2}

services:
  wash: {dist: constant, value: 5}
examples/yaml/simpy/carwash.yaml:machines-wash
wash:
  service: wash
  payload:
    event_type: washed
    dirt_removed_pct: {gen: integer, bounds: [50, 99]}

add_resource and add_service declare the machines and the wash time, and the wash task publishes dirt_removed_pct from a template.

examples/builder/simpy/carwash_example.py:machines

app.add_service("wash", dist="constant", value=5)

wash_payload = Template(
    {
        "event_type": "washed",
        "dirt_removed_pct": {"gen": "integer", "bounds": [50, 99]},
    },
    # The name gives the random sequence the YAML version's payload draws from
    name="tasks.wash",
)

@app.task(name="wash", service_id="wash")
def wash(task_id):
    """Washes the car."""
    return wash_payload

The low-level version has SimPy's simpy.Resource for the machines and a wash function that draws the dirt removed from desflow's Sampler.

dirt = sampler.generator("tasks.wash.payload.dirt_removed_pct")

numbers = {task: itertools.count() for task in ("car", "washing", "wash")}

def wash(name):
    number = next(numbers["wash"])
    publish(
        name,
        "wash",
        number,
        {
            "path_id": WASH,
            "sim_id": "Carwash",
            "service": "wash",
            "status": "started",

    )

docs.title: Car Is Washed
docs.text:
SimPy's car requests a machine, keeps it while the wash runs, and then leaves.

docs/snippets/simpy/carwash.py:car-is-washed
def car(env, name, cw):
    """The car process (each car has a ``name``) arrives at the carwash
    (``cw``) and requests a cleaning machine.

    It then starts the washing process, waits for it to finish and
    leaves to never come back ...

    """
    print(f'{name} arrives at the carwash at {env.now:.2f}.')
    with cw.machine.request() as request:
        yield request

        print(f'{name} enters the carwash at {env.now:.2f}.')
        yield env.process(cw.wash(name))

        print(f'{name} leaves the carwash at {env.now:.2f}.')
YAMLBuilderLow-level

car takes a machine with seize: machine, which keeps the unit after the task ends. washing waits for the wash task to finish with wait: {task: wash}, and then gives the machine back with release: machine.

examples/yaml/simpy/carwash.yaml:car-is-washed
tasks:
  car:
    seize: machine
    payload: {event_type: enters}
    next: washing
  # The car keeps its machine until the wash, a task of its own, has finished
  washing:
    wait: {task: wash}
    payload: {event_type: leaves}
    release: machine

The car and washing tasks take seize, wait and release as the YAML does.

examples/builder/simpy/carwash_example.py:car-is-washed
@app.task(name="car", seize="machine", next="washing")
def car(task_id):
    """Takes a machine and keeps it."""
    return {"event_type": "enters"}

# The car keeps its machine until the wash, a task of its own, has finished
@app.task(name="washing", wait={"task": "wash"}, release="machine")
def washing(task_id):
    """Leaves once its wash has finished."""
    return {"event_type": "leaves"}

The car function is SimPy's with machine.request() block. It runs the wash as a process and publishes the records of the three tasks.

examples/low-level/simpy/carwash_example.py:car-is-washed
def car(name):
    number = next(numbers["car"])
    with machine.request() as request:
        publish(name, "car", number, {"status": "queued"})
        yield request
        publish(name, "car", number, {"status": "started"})
        publish(name, "car", number, {"event_type": "enters"})
        # The car keeps its machine until the wash has finished
        waiting = next(numbers["washing"])
        publish(name, "washing", waiting, {"status": "queued"})
        yield env.process(wash(name))
        publish(name, "washing", waiting, {"status": "started"})
        publish(name, "washing", waiting, {"event_type": "leaves"})

docs.title: Cars Arrive
docs.text:
SimPy's setup starts four cars at time 0 and then a car after each gap of 5 to 9 minutes.

docs/snippets/simpy/carwash.py:cars-arrive
def setup(env, num_machines, washtime, t_inter):
    """Create a carwash, a number of initial cars and keep creating cars
    approx. every ``t_inter`` minutes."""
    # Create the carwash
    carwash = Carwash(env, num_machines, washtime)

    car_count = itertools.count()

    # Create 4 initial cars
    for _ in range(4):
        env.process(car(env, f'Car {next(car_count)}', carwash))

    # Create more cars while the simulation is running
    while True:
        yield env.timeout(random.randint(t_inter - 2, t_inter + 2))
        env.process(car(env, f'Car {next(car_count)}', carwash))

docs.title: Check the Result
docs.text:
Six cars enter the carwash in the 20 seconds. Cars 0 to 3 are waiting at time 0, car 4 arrives at 9 seconds and car 5 at 15 seconds. Cars 0 and 1 finish washing at 5 seconds, cars 2 and 3 at 10 seconds and car 4 at 15 seconds. Car 5 starts its wash at 15 seconds and would finish at 20 seconds, when the run ends, so the records show no wash finished for it.

SimPy's example prints the percentage of dirt removed in a line of text. Here it is the dirt_removed_pct field of each washed record. desflow draws each random value from its own stream, named by the place where the value is used, such as arrivals.cars.gap. A seed of 42 therefore gives different numbers from SimPy's random.seed(42). The system is the same. The figures are not.

examples/yaml/simpy/carwash.yaml
# Carwash: SimPy's carwash.py example, in YAML.
#
# The YAML version of carwash_example.py, which --api builder downloads. A carwash has
# two washing machines. Four cars wait when it opens. A car takes a machine, keeps it
# while the wash runs (a task of its own that removes 50 to 99 percent of the dirt),
# and then leaves.
#
# SimPy's example counts minutes, and here each of its minutes is one second. So a car
# arrives every 5 to 9 seconds, a wash takes 5 seconds, and the run ends after 20
# seconds, SimPy's 20 minutes. Each value is drawn from desflow's random sequence for
# its place in the file, so the numbers differ from those SimPy prints.
#
# Needs no containers. Runs unpaced and ends after 20 simulation seconds.
# Run it from its folder with: desflow run carwash.yaml

simulation: {sim_id: Carwash, factor: 0, random_seed: 42}

egress:
  - {type: Console}

resources:
  machine: {current_cap: 2}

services:
  wash: {dist: constant, value: 5}

arrivals:
  cars:
    initial: 4
    gap: {gen: integer, bounds: [5, 9]}
    spawn: car
    key: {gen: sequence, format: "Car {}"}

tasks:
  car:
    seize: machine
    payload: {event_type: enters}
    next: washing
  # The car keeps its machine until the wash, a task of its own, has finished
  washing:
    wait: {task: wash}
    payload: {event_type: leaves}
    release: machine
  wash:
    service: wash
    payload:
      event_type: washed
      dirt_removed_pct: {gen: integer, bounds: [50, 99]}

run: {until: 20}

The script builds the model with the builder API.

examples/builder/simpy/carwash_example.py
"""Carwash: SimPy's carwash.py example, builder API.

A carwash has two washing machines. Four cars wait when it opens. A car takes a
machine, keeps it while the wash runs (a task of its own that removes 50 to 99 percent
of the dirt), and then leaves.

SimPy's example counts minutes, and here each of its minutes is one second. So a car
arrives every 5 to 9 seconds, a wash takes 5 seconds, and the run ends after 20
seconds, SimPy's 20 minutes. Each value is drawn from desflow's random sequence for its
place in the model, so the numbers differ from those SimPy prints.

Needs no containers. Runs unpaced and ends after 20 simulation seconds.
"""

import logging

from desflow import ConsoleEgress, SimulationContext
from desflow.values import Template, generator


def build(size: int = 4) -> SimulationContext:
    """Builds the carwash, with `size` cars waiting when it opens."""
    app = SimulationContext(sim_id="Carwash", factor=0, random_seed=42)
    app.add_egress(ConsoleEgress())
    app.add_resource("machine", current_cap=2)
    app.add_service("wash", dist="constant", value=5)
    app.add_arrival(
        "cars",
        gap=generator({"gen": "integer", "bounds": [5, 9]}),
        key=lambda n: "Car {}".format(n - 1),
        initial=size,
        spawn="car",
    )

    @app.task(name="car", seize="machine", next="washing")
    def car(task_id):
        """Takes a machine and keeps it."""
        return {"event_type": "enters"}

    # The car keeps its machine until the wash, a task of its own, has finished
    @app.task(name="washing", wait={"task": "wash"}, release="machine")
    def washing(task_id):
        """Leaves once its wash has finished."""
        return {"event_type": "leaves"}


    wash_payload = Template(
        {
            "event_type": "washed",
            "dirt_removed_pct": {"gen": "integer", "bounds": [50, 99]},
        },
        # The name gives the random sequence the YAML version's payload draws from
        name="tasks.wash",
    )

    @app.task(name="wash", service_id="wash")
    def wash(task_id):
        """Washes the car."""
        return wash_payload


    return app


app = build()


def run(model: SimulationContext = app) -> None:
    """Runs 20 simulation seconds."""
    model.run(until=20)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    run()

The script wires the model by hand on DynamicRealtimeEnvironment, with SimPy's own processes.

examples/low-level/simpy/carwash_example.py
"""Carwash: SimPy's carwash.py example, low-level API.

The low-level version of `builder/simpy/carwash_example.py`: SimPy's own processes on
a `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment`. They publish with `publish_event` the records that the
YAML and builder versions publish: each task's `queued` and `started`, its own
events, and the number of the task's instance. A carwash has two washing machines.
Four cars wait when it opens. A car takes a machine, keeps it while the wash runs
(removing 50 to 99 percent of the dirt), and then leaves.

SimPy's example counts minutes, and here each of its minutes is one second. So a car
arrives every 5 to 9 seconds, a wash takes 5 seconds, and the run ends after 20
seconds, SimPy's 20 minutes. Each value is drawn from desflow's `Sampler`, from the
random sequence the YAML and builder versions use for the same place, so the three
versions publish the same records.

Needs no containers. Runs unpaced and ends after 20 simulation seconds.
"""

import itertools
import logging

import simpy

from desflow import ConsoleEgress, DynamicRealtimeEnvironment, Sampler

NUM_MACHINES = 2
WASHTIME = 5
UNTIL = 20
WASH = "Carwash.service.wash"  # the service that the wash's started record names


def build(env: DynamicRealtimeEnvironment, size: int = 4) -> None:
    """Starts the carwash on `env`, with `size` cars waiting when it opens."""
    sampler = Sampler(seed=42)
    gaps = sampler.generator("arrivals.cars.gap")
    dirt = sampler.generator("tasks.wash.payload.dirt_removed_pct")
    machine = simpy.Resource(env, NUM_MACHINES)
    numbers = {task: itertools.count() for task in ("car", "washing", "wash")}

    def publish(name, task, number, value):
        env.publish_event(name, value, task=task, instance=number)

    def wash(name):
        number = next(numbers["wash"])
        publish(
            name,
            "wash",
            number,
            {
                "path_id": WASH,
                "sim_id": "Carwash",
                "service": "wash",
                "status": "started",
            },
        )
        yield env.timeout(WASHTIME)
        removed = int(dirt.integers(50, 100))
        publish(
            name, "wash", number, {"event_type": "washed", "dirt_removed_pct": removed}
        )


    def car(name):
        number = next(numbers["car"])
        with machine.request() as request:
            publish(name, "car", number, {"status": "queued"})
            yield request
            publish(name, "car", number, {"status": "started"})
            publish(name, "car", number, {"event_type": "enters"})
            # The car keeps its machine until the wash has finished
            waiting = next(numbers["washing"])
            publish(name, "washing", waiting, {"status": "queued"})
            yield env.process(wash(name))
            publish(name, "washing", waiting, {"status": "started"})
            publish(name, "washing", waiting, {"event_type": "leaves"})


    def setup():
        for i in range(size):
            env.process(car(f"Car {i}"))
        i = size
        while True:
            yield env.timeout(int(gaps.integers(5, 10)))
            env.process(car(f"Car {i}"))
            i += 1

    env.process(setup())


def run() -> None:
    """Runs 20 simulation seconds."""
    env = DynamicRealtimeEnvironment(factor=0)
    env.setup_egress([ConsoleEgress()])
    build(env)
    try:
        env.run(until=UNTIL)
    finally:
        env.teardown()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    run()

"""
Carwash example.

Covers:

- Waiting for other processes
- Resources: Resource

Scenario:
  A carwash has a limited number of washing machines and defines
  a washing processes that takes some (random) time.

  Car processes arrive at the carwash at a random time. If one washing
  machine is available, they start the washing process and wait for it
  to finish. If not, they wait until they can use one.

"""

import itertools
import random

import simpy

# fmt: off
RANDOM_SEED = 42
NUM_MACHINES = 2  # Number of machines in the carwash
WASHTIME = 5      # Minutes it takes to clean a car
T_INTER = 7       # Create a car every ~7 minutes
SIM_TIME = 20     # Simulation time in minutes
# fmt: on


class Carwash:
    """A carwash has a limited number of machines (``NUM_MACHINES``) to
    clean cars in parallel.

    Cars have to request one of the machines. When they got one, they
    can start the washing processes and wait for it to finish (which
    takes ``washtime`` minutes).

    """

    def __init__(self, env, num_machines, washtime):
        self.env = env
        self.machine = simpy.Resource(env, num_machines)
        self.washtime = washtime

    def wash(self, car):
        """The washing processes. It takes a ``car`` processes and tries
        to clean it."""
        yield self.env.timeout(self.washtime)
        pct_dirt = random.randint(50, 99)
        print(f"Carwash removed {pct_dirt}% of {car}'s dirt.")


def car(env, name, cw):
    """The car process (each car has a ``name``) arrives at the carwash
    (``cw``) and requests a cleaning machine.

    It then starts the washing process, waits for it to finish and
    leaves to never come back ...

    """
    print(f'{name} arrives at the carwash at {env.now:.2f}.')
    with cw.machine.request() as request:
        yield request

        print(f'{name} enters the carwash at {env.now:.2f}.')
        yield env.process(cw.wash(name))

        print(f'{name} leaves the carwash at {env.now:.2f}.')


def setup(env, num_machines, washtime, t_inter):
    """Create a carwash, a number of initial cars and keep creating cars
    approx. every ``t_inter`` minutes."""
    # Create the carwash
    carwash = Carwash(env, num_machines, washtime)

    car_count = itertools.count()

    # Create 4 initial cars
    for _ in range(4):
        env.process(car(env, f'Car {next(car_count)}', carwash))

    # Create more cars while the simulation is running
    while True:
        yield env.timeout(random.randint(t_inter - 2, t_inter + 2))
        env.process(car(env, f'Car {next(car_count)}', carwash))


# Setup and start the simulation
print('Carwash')
print('Check out http://youtu.be/fXXmeP9TvBg while simulating ... ;-)')
random.seed(RANDOM_SEED)  # This helps to reproduce the results

# Create an environment and start the setup process
env = simpy.Environment()
env.process(setup(env, NUM_MACHINES, WASHTIME, T_INTER))

# Execute!
env.run(until=SIM_TIME)

docs.title: Gas Station Refueling
docs.text: Cars take fuel from a station's tank, and a control process calls a tank truck when the tank runs low. This is SimPy's Gas Station Refueling example, written in desflow.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
SimPy's gas station has two pumps and a tank of 200 litres. A car arrives every 30 to 300 seconds with 5 to 25 litres left in its 50 litre tank. It waits for a pump, takes the fuel it needs from the station's tank, and refuels at 2 litres a second. A control process checks the tank every 10 seconds. When the tank is below 25 percent, it calls a tank truck, which arrives 300 seconds later and fills the tank. The run lasts 1000 seconds.

The example needs only desflow, which each Quick Start in Run It installs, and no other service. desflow examples get simpy-gas-station-refuel --api yaml downloads it, as Get an Example shows. SimPy Examples says how these pages read SimPy's times and numbers. SimPy's own page for the example is on its documentation site.

docs.title: Car Refuels
docs.text:
SimPy's car requests a pump, takes the fuel it needs from the tank, and refuels at 2 litres a second.

docs/snippets/simpy/gas_station_refuel.py:car-refuels
def car(name, env, gas_station, station_tank):
    """A car arrives at the gas station for refueling.

    It requests one of the gas station's fuel pumps and tries to get the
    desired amount of fuel from it. If the station's fuel tank is
    depleted, the car has to wait for the tank truck to arrive.

    """
    car_tank_level = random.randint(*CAR_TANK_LEVEL)
    print(f'{env.now:6.1f} s: {name} arrived at gas station')
    with gas_station.request() as req:
        # Request one of the gas pumps
        yield req

        # Get the required amount of fuel
        fuel_required = CAR_TANK_SIZE - car_tank_level
        yield station_tank.get(fuel_required)

        # The "actual" refueling process takes some time
        yield env.timeout(fuel_required / REFUELING_SPEED)

        print(f'{env.now:6.1f} s: {name} refueled with {fuel_required:.1f}L')
YAMLBuilderLow-level

pumps is a resource with two units and tank is a container of 200 litres, full at the start. The car task takes a pump, gets 50 - attr.level litres from the tank, and refuels for (50 - attr.level) / 2 seconds. attr.level is the fuel the car has left.

examples/yaml/simpy/gas_station_refuel.yaml:pumps-and-tank
resources:
  pumps: {current_cap: 2}

containers:
  tank: {current_cap: 200, level: 200}
examples/yaml/simpy/gas_station_refuel.yaml:car-refuels
car:
  resource: pumps
  get: {container: tank, amount: "50 - attr.level"}
  service_time: "(50 - attr.level) / 2"
  payload:
    event_type: refueled
    litres: {gen: expr, expr: "50 - attr.level"}

add_resource and add_container declare the pumps and the tank. The car task takes get and service_time as expressions on the car's attribute.

examples/builder/simpy/gas_station_refuel_example.py:pumps-and-tank

app.add_container("tank", current_cap=200, level=200)

car_payload = Template(
    {
        "event_type": "refueled",
        "litres": {"gen": "expr", "expr": "50 - attr.level"},
    },
    name="car",
)

@app.task(
    name="car",
    resource_id="pumps",
    get={"container": "tank", "amount": "50 - attr.level"},
    service_time="(50 - attr.level) / 2",
)
def car(task_id):
    """Refuels at a pump."""
    return car_payload

The low-level version has SimPy's simpy.Resource and simpy.Container, and SimPy's car function with records published for it.

examples/low-level/simpy/gas_station_refuel_example.py:pumps-and-tank

station_tank = simpy.Container(env, STATION_TANK_SIZE, init=STATION_TANK_SIZE)
examples/low-level/simpy/gas_station_refuel_example.py:car-refuels
def car(name, car_tank_level):
    number = next(numbers["car"])
    with gas_station.request() as req:
        publish(name, "car", number, {"status": "queued"})
        yield req
        fuel_required = CAR_TANK_SIZE - car_tank_level
        yield station_tank.get(fuel_required)
        publish(name, "car", number, {"status": "started"})
        yield env.timeout(fuel_required / REFUELING_SPEED)
        publish(
            name, "car", number, {"event_type": "refueled", "litres": fuel_required}
        )

docs.title: Control Calls the Truck
docs.text:
SimPy's gas_station_control checks the tank every 10 seconds and, below 25 percent, calls the truck and waits for it.

docs/snippets/simpy/gas_station_refuel.py:control-calls-truck
def gas_station_control(env, station_tank):
    """Periodically check the level of the gas station tank and call the tank
    truck if the level falls below a threshold."""
    while True:
        if station_tank.level / station_tank.capacity * 100 < THRESHOLD:
            # We need to call the tank truck now!
            print(f'{env.now:6.1f} s: Calling tank truck')
            # Wait for the tank truck to arrive and refuel the station tank
            yield env.process(tank_truck(env, station_tank))

        yield env.timeout(10)  # Check every 10 seconds
YAMLBuilderLow-level

The control task checks level.tank / 200 * 100 < 25 in its next rule. When the tank is low it goes to call_truck, and then to await_truck, which waits for the truck task to finish. Otherwise it goes to pause, which waits 10 seconds and returns to control.

examples/yaml/simpy/gas_station_refuel.yaml:control-calls-truck
control:
  payload: {event_type: checked}
  next:
    when:
      - {condition: "level.tank / 200 * 100 < 25", task: call_truck}
    default: pause
call_truck:
  payload: {event_type: truck_called}
  next: await_truck
await_truck:
  wait: {task: truck}
  payload: {event_type: truck_returned}
  next: pause
examples/yaml/simpy/gas_station_refuel.yaml:pause
pause:
  service_time: 10
  payload: {event_type: waited}
  next: control

The same tasks, with next and wait as in the YAML.

examples/builder/simpy/gas_station_refuel_example.py:control-calls-truck
@app.task(
    name="control",
    next={
        "when": [
            {"condition": "level.tank / 200 * 100 < 25", "task": "call_truck"}
        ],
        "default": "pause",
    },
)
def control(task_id):
    """Checks the level of the tank."""
    return {"event_type": "checked"}

@app.task(name="call_truck", next="await_truck")
def call_truck(task_id):
    """Calls the tank truck."""
    return {"event_type": "truck_called"}

@app.task(name="await_truck", wait={"task": "truck"}, next="pause")
def await_truck(task_id):
    """Waits for the tank truck."""
    return {"event_type": "truck_returned"}
examples/builder/simpy/gas_station_refuel_example.py:pause
@app.task(name="pause", service_time=10, next="control")
def pause(task_id):
    """Waits until the next check."""
    return {"event_type": "waited"}

gas_station_control is SimPy's loop. It runs tank_truck as a process and waits for it.

examples/low-level/simpy/gas_station_refuel_example.py:control-calls-truck
def gas_station_control(name):
    while True:
        publish(
            name, "control", next(numbers["control"]), {"event_type": "checked"}
        )
        if station_tank.level / station_tank.capacity * 100 < THRESHOLD:
            call = next(numbers["call_truck"])
            publish(name, "call_truck", call, {"event_type": "truck_called"})
            waiting = next(numbers["await_truck"])
            publish(name, "await_truck", waiting, {"status": "queued"})
            yield env.process(tank_truck(name))
            publish(name, "await_truck", waiting, {"status": "started"})
            publish(name, "await_truck", waiting, {"event_type": "truck_returned"})
        pause = next(numbers["pause"])
        publish(name, "pause", pause, {"status": "started"})
        yield env.timeout(10)
        publish(name, "pause", pause, {"event_type": "waited"})

docs.title: Check the Result
docs.text:
Five cars refuel in the 1000 seconds. The control task finds the tank below 25 percent at 820 seconds and calls the truck. The truck needs 300 seconds, so it would arrive at 1120 seconds, after the run ends, and the records show no truck arrival.

In SimPy's output, below, the truck is called at 460 seconds and arrives at 760 seconds. Here the cars arrive at other times, so the tank is low later. desflow draws each random value from its own stream, named by the place where the value is used, such as arrivals.cars.gap. A seed of 42 therefore gives different numbers from SimPy's random.seed(42). The system is the same. The figures are not.

# Gas Station Refueling: SimPy's gas_station_refuel.py example, in YAML.
#
# The YAML version of gas_station_refuel_example.py, which --api builder downloads. A
# gas station has two pumps and a tank of 200 litres. A car arrives every 30 to 300
# seconds with 5 to 25 litres left in its 50 litre tank. It waits for a pump, takes
# the fuel it needs from the station's tank and refuels at 2 litres a second. A control
# task checks the tank every 10 seconds, and when it is below 25 percent it calls a
# tank truck, which arrives 300 seconds later and fills the tank.
#
# Each value is drawn from desflow's random sequence for its place in the file, so the
# numbers differ from those SimPy prints.
#
# Needs no containers. Runs unpaced and ends after 1000 simulation seconds.
# Run it from its folder with: desflow run gas_station_refuel.yaml

simulation: {sim_id: GasStation, factor: 0, random_seed: 42}

egress:
  - {type: Console}

resources:
  pumps: {current_cap: 2}

containers:
  tank: {current_cap: 200, level: 200}

arrivals:
  control: {initial: 1, spawn: control}
  cars:
    gap: {gen: integer, bounds: [30, 300]}
    spawn: car
    key: {gen: sequence, format: "Car {}"}
    attributes:
      level: {gen: integer, bounds: [5, 25]}

tasks:
  car:
    resource: pumps
    get: {container: tank, amount: "50 - attr.level"}
    service_time: "(50 - attr.level) / 2"
    payload:
      event_type: refueled
      litres: {gen: expr, expr: "50 - attr.level"}
  control:
    payload: {event_type: checked}
    next:
      when:
        - {condition: "level.tank / 200 * 100 < 25", task: call_truck}
      default: pause
  call_truck:
    payload: {event_type: truck_called}
    next: await_truck
  await_truck:
    wait: {task: truck}
    payload: {event_type: truck_returned}
    next: pause
  truck:
    service_time: 300
    put: {container: tank, amount: "200 - level.tank"}
    payload:
      event_type: truck_arrived
      litres: {gen: expr, expr: "200 - level.tank"}
  pause:
    service_time: 10
    payload: {event_type: waited}
    next: control

run: {until: 1000}

examples/builder/simpy/gas_station_refuel_example.py
"""Gas Station Refueling: SimPy's gas_station_refuel.py example, builder API.

A gas station has two pumps and a tank of 200 litres. A car arrives every 30 to 300
seconds with 5 to 25 litres left in its 50 litre tank. It waits for a pump, takes the
fuel it needs from the station's tank and refuels at 2 litres a second. A control task
checks the tank every 10 seconds, and when it is below 25 percent it calls a tank
truck, which arrives 300 seconds later and fills the tank.

Each value is drawn from desflow's random sequence for its place in the model, so the
numbers differ from those SimPy prints.

Needs no containers. Runs unpaced and ends after 1000 simulation seconds.
"""

import logging

from desflow import ConsoleEgress, SimulationContext
from desflow.values import Template, generator


def build() -> SimulationContext:
    """Builds the gas station."""
    app = SimulationContext(sim_id="GasStation", factor=0, random_seed=42)
    app.add_egress(ConsoleEgress())
    app.add_resource("pumps", current_cap=2)
    app.add_container("tank", current_cap=200, level=200)
    app.add_initial_arrival("control", 1, spawn="control")
    app.add_arrival(
        "cars",
        gap=generator({"gen": "integer", "bounds": [30, 300]}),
        key=lambda n: "Car {}".format(n - 1),
        attributes={"level": generator({"gen": "integer", "bounds": [5, 25]})},
        spawn="car",
    )
    car_payload = Template(
        {
            "event_type": "refueled",
            "litres": {"gen": "expr", "expr": "50 - attr.level"},
        },
        name="car",
    )

    @app.task(
        name="car",
        resource_id="pumps",
        get={"container": "tank", "amount": "50 - attr.level"},
        service_time="(50 - attr.level) / 2",
    )
    def car(task_id):
        """Refuels at a pump."""
        return car_payload


    @app.task(
        name="control",
        next={
            "when": [
                {"condition": "level.tank / 200 * 100 < 25", "task": "call_truck"}
            ],
            "default": "pause",
        },
    )
    def control(task_id):
        """Checks the level of the tank."""
        return {"event_type": "checked"}

    @app.task(name="call_truck", next="await_truck")
    def call_truck(task_id):
        """Calls the tank truck."""
        return {"event_type": "truck_called"}

    @app.task(name="await_truck", wait={"task": "truck"}, next="pause")
    def await_truck(task_id):
        """Waits for the tank truck."""
        return {"event_type": "truck_returned"}


    truck_payload = Template(
        {
            "event_type": "truck_arrived",
            "litres": {"gen": "expr", "expr": "200 - level.tank"},
        },
        name="truck",
    )

    @app.task(
        name="truck",
        service_time=300,
        put={"container": "tank", "amount": "200 - level.tank"},
    )
    def truck(task_id):
        """Fills the tank on arrival."""
        return truck_payload


    @app.task(name="pause", service_time=10, next="control")
    def pause(task_id):
        """Waits until the next check."""
        return {"event_type": "waited"}


    return app


app = build()


def run(model: SimulationContext = app) -> None:
    """Runs 1000 simulation seconds."""
    model.run(until=1000)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    run()

The script wires the model by hand on DynamicRealtimeEnvironment, with SimPy's own processes.

examples/low-level/simpy/gas_station_refuel_example.py
"""Gas Station Refueling: SimPy's gas_station_refuel.py example, low-level API.

The low-level version of `builder/simpy/gas_station_refuel_example.py`: SimPy's own
processes on a `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment`. They publish with `publish_event` the
records that the YAML and builder versions publish: each task's `queued` and
`started`, its own events, and the number of the task's instance. A gas station has
two pumps and a tank of 200 litres. A car arrives every 30 to 300 seconds with 5 to
25 litres left in its 50 litre tank. It waits for a pump, takes the fuel it needs
from the station's tank and refuels at 2 litres a second. A control process checks
the tank every 10 seconds, and when it is below 25 percent it calls a tank truck,
which arrives 300 seconds later and fills the tank.

Each value is drawn from desflow's `Sampler`, from the random sequence the YAML and
builder versions use for the same place, so the three versions publish the same
records.

Needs no containers. Runs unpaced and ends after 1000 simulation seconds.
"""

import itertools
import logging

import simpy

from desflow import ConsoleEgress, DynamicRealtimeEnvironment, Sampler

STATION_TANK_SIZE = 200  # litres
THRESHOLD = 25  # percent of the tank that calls the truck
CAR_TANK_SIZE = 50  # litres
REFUELING_SPEED = 2  # litres a second
TANK_TRUCK_TIME = 300  # seconds
UNTIL = 1000


def build(env: DynamicRealtimeEnvironment) -> None:
    """Starts the control process and the cars on `env`."""
    sampler = Sampler(seed=42)
    gaps = sampler.generator("arrivals.cars.gap")
    levels = sampler.generator("arrivals.cars.attributes.level")
    gas_station = simpy.Resource(env, 2)
    station_tank = simpy.Container(env, STATION_TANK_SIZE, init=STATION_TANK_SIZE)
    numbers = {
        task: itertools.count()
        for task in ("car", "control", "call_truck", "await_truck", "truck", "pause")
    }

    def publish(name, task, number, value):
        env.publish_event(name, value, task=task, instance=number)

    def car(name, car_tank_level):
        number = next(numbers["car"])
        with gas_station.request() as req:
            publish(name, "car", number, {"status": "queued"})
            yield req
            fuel_required = CAR_TANK_SIZE - car_tank_level
            yield station_tank.get(fuel_required)
            publish(name, "car", number, {"status": "started"})
            yield env.timeout(fuel_required / REFUELING_SPEED)
            publish(
                name, "car", number, {"event_type": "refueled", "litres": fuel_required}
            )


    def tank_truck(name):
        number = next(numbers["truck"])
        publish(name, "truck", number, {"status": "started"})
        yield env.timeout(TANK_TRUCK_TIME)
        amount = station_tank.capacity - station_tank.level
        yield station_tank.put(amount)
        publish(
            name, "truck", number, {"event_type": "truck_arrived", "litres": amount}
        )


    def gas_station_control(name):
        while True:
            publish(
                name, "control", next(numbers["control"]), {"event_type": "checked"}
            )
            if station_tank.level / station_tank.capacity * 100 < THRESHOLD:
                call = next(numbers["call_truck"])
                publish(name, "call_truck", call, {"event_type": "truck_called"})
                waiting = next(numbers["await_truck"])
                publish(name, "await_truck", waiting, {"status": "queued"})
                yield env.process(tank_truck(name))
                publish(name, "await_truck", waiting, {"status": "started"})
                publish(name, "await_truck", waiting, {"event_type": "truck_returned"})
            pause = next(numbers["pause"])
            publish(name, "pause", pause, {"status": "started"})
            yield env.timeout(10)
            publish(name, "pause", pause, {"event_type": "waited"})


    def car_generator():
        for i in itertools.count():
            yield env.timeout(int(gaps.integers(30, 301)))
            env.process(car(f"Car {i}", int(levels.integers(5, 26))))

    env.process(gas_station_control("control-1"))
    env.process(car_generator())


def run() -> None:
    """Runs 1000 simulation seconds."""
    env = DynamicRealtimeEnvironment(factor=0)
    env.setup_egress([ConsoleEgress()])
    build(env)
    try:
        env.run(until=UNTIL)
    finally:
        env.teardown()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    run()

"""
Gas Station Refueling example

Covers:

- Resources: Resource
- Resources: Container
- Waiting for other processes

Scenario:
  A gas station has a limited number of gas pumps that share a common
  fuel reservoir. Cars randomly arrive at the gas station, request one
  of the fuel pumps and start refueling from that reservoir.

  A gas station control process observes the gas station's fuel level
  and calls a tank truck for refueling if the station's level drops
  below a threshold.

"""

import itertools
import random

import simpy

# fmt: off
RANDOM_SEED = 42
STATION_TANK_SIZE = 200    # Size of the gas station tank (liters)
THRESHOLD = 25             # Station tank minimum level (% of full)
CAR_TANK_SIZE = 50         # Size of car fuel tanks (liters)
CAR_TANK_LEVEL = [5, 25]   # Min/max levels of car fuel tanks (liters)
REFUELING_SPEED = 2        # Rate of refuelling car fuel tank (liters / second)
TANK_TRUCK_TIME = 300      # Time it takes tank truck to arrive (seconds)
T_INTER = [30, 300]        # Interval between car arrivals [min, max] (seconds)
SIM_TIME = 1000            # Simulation time (seconds)
# fmt: on


def car(name, env, gas_station, station_tank):
    """A car arrives at the gas station for refueling.

    It requests one of the gas station's fuel pumps and tries to get the
    desired amount of fuel from it. If the station's fuel tank is
    depleted, the car has to wait for the tank truck to arrive.

    """
    car_tank_level = random.randint(*CAR_TANK_LEVEL)
    print(f'{env.now:6.1f} s: {name} arrived at gas station')
    with gas_station.request() as req:
        # Request one of the gas pumps
        yield req

        # Get the required amount of fuel
        fuel_required = CAR_TANK_SIZE - car_tank_level
        yield station_tank.get(fuel_required)

        # The "actual" refueling process takes some time
        yield env.timeout(fuel_required / REFUELING_SPEED)

        print(f'{env.now:6.1f} s: {name} refueled with {fuel_required:.1f}L')


def gas_station_control(env, station_tank):
    """Periodically check the level of the gas station tank and call the tank
    truck if the level falls below a threshold."""
    while True:
        if station_tank.level / station_tank.capacity * 100 < THRESHOLD:
            # We need to call the tank truck now!
            print(f'{env.now:6.1f} s: Calling tank truck')
            # Wait for the tank truck to arrive and refuel the station tank
            yield env.process(tank_truck(env, station_tank))

        yield env.timeout(10)  # Check every 10 seconds


def tank_truck(env, station_tank):
    """Arrives at the gas station after a certain delay and refuels it."""
    yield env.timeout(TANK_TRUCK_TIME)
    amount = station_tank.capacity - station_tank.level
    station_tank.put(amount)
    print(
        f'{env.now:6.1f} s: Tank truck arrived and refuelled station with {amount:.1f}L'
    )


def car_generator(env, gas_station, station_tank):
    """Generate new cars that arrive at the gas station."""
    for i in itertools.count():
        yield env.timeout(random.randint(*T_INTER))
        env.process(car(f'Car {i}', env, gas_station, station_tank))


# Setup and start the simulation
print('Gas Station refuelling')
random.seed(RANDOM_SEED)

# Create environment and start processes
env = simpy.Environment()
gas_station = simpy.Resource(env, 2)
station_tank = simpy.Container(env, STATION_TANK_SIZE, init=STATION_TANK_SIZE)
env.process(gas_station_control(env, station_tank))
env.process(car_generator(env, gas_station, station_tank))

# Execute!
env.run(until=SIM_TIME)

docs.title: Event Latency
docs.text: A sender puts a message on a cable every 5 seconds, the cable delivers it 10 seconds later, and a receiver takes each message as it arrives. This is SimPy's Event Latency example, written in desflow.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
SimPy's example keeps the delay of a cable outside the sender and the receiver. The sender puts a message on the cable every 5 time units. The cable holds each message for 10 time units and then puts it into a store. The receiver takes each message from the store. The run lasts 100 time units. SimPy counts no unit, and desflow reads each unit as one second.

Nothing in this example is random, so the times are the same as SimPy's.

The example needs only desflow, which each Quick Start in Run It installs, and no other service. desflow examples get simpy-latency --api yaml downloads it, as Get an Example shows. SimPy Examples says how these pages read SimPy's times and numbers. SimPy's own page for the example is on its documentation site.

docs.title: Cable Delays Messages
docs.text:
SimPy's Cable class starts a process for each message. The process waits for the delay and then puts the message into a store. The sender and the receiver never see the delay.

docs/snippets/simpy/latency.py:cable-delays
class Cable:
    """This class represents the propagation through a cable."""

    def __init__(self, env, delay):
        self.env = env
        self.delay = delay
        self.store = simpy.Store(env)

    def latency(self, value):
        yield self.env.timeout(self.delay)
        self.store.put(value)

    def put(self, value):
        self.env.process(self.latency(value))

    def get(self):
        return self.store.get()

examples/low-level/simpy/latency_example.py:cable-delays
class Cable:
    """A cable that delivers each value `delay` seconds after it was put in."""

    def __init__(self, env: DynamicRealtimeEnvironment, delay: float):
        self.env = env
        self.delay = delay
        self.store = simpy.Store(env)
        self.numbers = itertools.count(1)
        self.instances = itertools.count()

    def latency(self, name, value):
        number = next(self.instances)

        def publish(record):
            self.env.publish_event(name, record, task="latency", instance=number)

        publish({"status": "started"})
        yield self.env.timeout(self.delay)
        done = self.store.put(value)
        done.callbacks.append(lambda _: publish({"event_type": "delivered"}))

    def put(self, value):
        """Sends `value`, which travels on its own."""
        name = f"latency-{next(self.numbers)}"
        self.env.process(self.latency(name, value))

    def get(self):
        """The next value delivered."""
        return self.store.get()

The script builds the model with the builder API.

examples/builder/simpy/latency_example.py
"""Event Latency: SimPy's latency.py example, builder API.

A sender sends a message every 5 seconds over a cable. The cable delivers each message
into a store 10 seconds later, and a receiver takes each message as it arrives.

Needs no containers. Runs unpaced and ends after 100 simulation seconds.
"""

import logging

from desflow import ConsoleEgress, SimulationContext
from desflow.values import Template, generator


def build(size: int = 1) -> SimulationContext:
    """Builds the cable, with `size` receivers."""
    app = SimulationContext(sim_id="Cable", factor=0, random_seed=42)
    app.add_egress(ConsoleEgress())
    app.add_store("cable")
    app.add_arrival("sender", "constant", value=5, spawn="send")
    app.add_initial_arrival("receiver", size, spawn="receive")

    # Each message travels on its own, so the sender goes on at once
    @app.task(
        name="send",
        spawn={
            "task": "latency",
            "args": {
                "msg": generator(
                    {
                        "gen": "format",
                        "template": "Sender sent this at {now:g}",
                        "names": {"now": {"gen": "expr", "expr": "t"}},
                    }
                )
            },
        },
    )
    def send(task_id):
        """Sends a message."""
        return {"event_type": "sent"}


    @app.task(
        name="latency",
        service_time=10,
        put={"store": "cable", "item": generator({"gen": "expr", "expr": "arg.msg"})},
    )
    def latency(task_id):
        """Delivers the message into the cable's store after the delay."""
        return {"event_type": "delivered"}


    receive_payload = Template(
        {"event_type": "received", "msg": {"gen": "expr", "expr": "item"}},
        name="receive",
    )

    @app.task(name="receive", get={"store": "cable"}, next="receive")
    def receive(task_id):
        """Takes the next message."""
        return receive_payload


    return app


app = build()


def run(model: SimulationContext = app) -> None:
    """Runs 100 simulation seconds."""
    model.run(until=100)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    run()

The script wires the model by hand on DynamicRealtimeEnvironment, with SimPy's own processes.

examples/low-level/simpy/latency_example.py
"""Event Latency: SimPy's latency.py example, low-level API.

The low-level version of `builder/simpy/latency_example.py`: SimPy's own `Cable`,
sender and receiver on a `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment`. They publish with
`publish_event` the records that the YAML and builder versions publish: each task's
`queued` and `started`, its own events, and the number of the task's instance. A
sender sends a message every 5 seconds over a cable. The cable delivers each message
into a store 10 seconds later, and a receiver takes each message as it arrives.

Needs no containers. Runs unpaced and ends after 100 simulation seconds.
"""

import itertools
import logging

import simpy

from desflow import ConsoleEgress, DynamicRealtimeEnvironment

UNTIL = 100


class Cable:
    """A cable that delivers each value `delay` seconds after it was put in."""

    def __init__(self, env: DynamicRealtimeEnvironment, delay: float):
        self.env = env
        self.delay = delay
        self.store = simpy.Store(env)
        self.numbers = itertools.count(1)
        self.instances = itertools.count()

    def latency(self, name, value):
        number = next(self.instances)

        def publish(record):
            self.env.publish_event(name, record, task="latency", instance=number)

        publish({"status": "started"})
        yield self.env.timeout(self.delay)
        done = self.store.put(value)
        done.callbacks.append(lambda _: publish({"event_type": "delivered"}))

    def put(self, value):
        """Sends `value`, which travels on its own."""
        name = f"latency-{next(self.numbers)}"
        self.env.process(self.latency(name, value))

    def get(self):
        """The next value delivered."""
        return self.store.get()


def build(env: DynamicRealtimeEnvironment, size: int = 1) -> None:
    """Starts the sender and `size` receivers on `env`."""
    cable = Cable(env, 10)
    gets = itertools.count()

    def sender():
        for number in itertools.count(1):
            yield env.timeout(5)
            env.publish_event(
                f"sender-{number}",
                {"event_type": "sent"},
                task="send",
                instance=number - 1,
            )
            cable.put(f"Sender sent this at {env.now:g}")


    def receiver(name):
        def publish(number, record):
            env.publish_event(name, record, task="receive", instance=number)

        while True:
            number = next(gets)  # each message is taken by a new instance
            publish(number, {"status": "queued"})
            msg = yield cable.get()
            publish(number, {"status": "started"})
            publish(number, {"event_type": "received", "msg": msg})


    env.process(sender())
    for number in range(1, size + 1):
        env.process(receiver(f"receiver-{number}"))


def run() -> None:
    """Runs 100 simulation seconds."""
    env = DynamicRealtimeEnvironment(factor=0)
    env.setup_egress([ConsoleEgress()])
    build(env)
    try:
        env.run(until=UNTIL)
    finally:
        env.teardown()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    run()

"""
Event Latency example

Covers:

- Resources: Store

Scenario:
  This example shows how to separate the time delay of events between
  processes from the processes themselves.

When Useful:
  When modeling physical things such as cables, RF propagation, etc.  it
  better encapsulation to keep this propagation mechanism outside of the
  sending and receiving processes.

  Can also be used to interconnect processes sending messages

Example by:
  Keith Smith

"""

import simpy

SIM_DURATION = 100


class Cable:
    """This class represents the propagation through a cable."""

    def __init__(self, env, delay):
        self.env = env
        self.delay = delay
        self.store = simpy.Store(env)

    def latency(self, value):
        yield self.env.timeout(self.delay)
        self.store.put(value)

    def put(self, value):
        self.env.process(self.latency(value))

    def get(self):
        return self.store.get()


def sender(env, cable):
    """A process which randomly generates messages."""
    while True:
        # wait for next transmission
        yield env.timeout(5)
        cable.put(f'Sender sent this at {env.now}')


def receiver(env, cable):
    """A process which consumes messages."""
    while True:
        # Get event for message pipe
        msg = yield cable.get()
        print(f'Received this at {env.now} while {msg}')


# Setup and start the simulation
print('Event Latency')
env = simpy.Environment()

cable = Cable(env, 10)
env.process(sender(env, cable))
env.process(receiver(env, cable))

env.run(until=SIM_DURATION)
