docs.title: Machine Shop
docs.text: Ten machines make parts and break down, and one repairman repairs them before doing other jobs. This is SimPy's Machine Shop example, written in desflow.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
SimPy's shop has 10 machines. Each makes parts without end. A part takes a normal time with a mean of 10 minutes and a standard deviation of 2, never below 0. Each machine breaks down after an exponential time with a mean of 300 minutes, unless it is already broken. A broken machine waits for the one repairman, at priority 1, for a 30 minute repair, and then finishes its part. Between repairs the repairman does other jobs of 30 minutes at priority 2. A repair preempts such a job, and the job resumes afterwards. The run lasts 4 weeks, which is 40320 minutes. desflow reads each of SimPy's minutes as one second.

SimPy breaks a machine by calling interrupt on the process that makes parts. The repair is then a request for the repairman, who is a resource that the other jobs use too. The example writes the breakdowns as tasks, so that the repair is an ordinary request at priority 1: each machine has a break_loop task that waits for the next failure and interrupts the machine's part task, and the part task starts the repair when it is interrupted.

The example needs only desflow, which each Quick Start in Run It installs, and no other service. desflow examples get simpy-machine-shop --api yaml downloads it, as Get an Example shows. SimPy Examples says how these pages read SimPy's times and numbers. SimPy's own page for the example is on its documentation site.

docs.title: Times Are Drawn
docs.text:
SimPy draws the times with two functions, one for the time of a part and one for the time to a failure. desflow draws each time where it is used: the part time on the part task and the time to a failure on the break_loop task, both shown in the next step. The shop's own settings come first.

docs/snippets/simpy/machine_shop.py:times-drawn
def time_per_part():
    """Return actual processing time for a concrete part."""
    t = random.normalvariate(PT_MEAN, PT_SIGMA)
    # The normalvariate can be negative, but we want only positive times.
    while t <= 0:
        t = random.normalvariate(PT_MEAN, PT_SIGMA)
    return t


def time_to_failure():
    """Return time until next failure for a machine."""
    return random.expovariate(BREAK_MEAN)
YAMLBuilderLow-level

repairman is a resource with one unit that serves a priority queue and lets a request of higher priority preempt the unit's user. repair_time is a service of 30 seconds. parts_made counts the parts of each machine, and target names the machine that a failure breaks.

examples/yaml/simpy/machine_shop.yaml:shop-settings
variables:
  target: -1
  parts_made: {}

resources:
  repairman: {current_cap: 1, queue: priority, preempt: true}

services:
  repair_time: {dist: constant, value: 30}

add_resource, add_variable and add_service declare the same parts.

examples/builder/simpy/machine_shop_example.py:shop-settings
app.add_resource("repairman", current_cap=1, queue="priority", preempt=True)
app.add_variable("target", -1)
app.add_variable("parts_made", {})
app.add_service("repair_time", dist="constant", value=30)

The low-level version has SimPy's PreemptiveResource for the repairman, and a DistributionConfig for each of the two times, so that it draws from the same streams as the other versions.

examples/low-level/simpy/machine_shop_example.py:shop-settings
sampler = Sampler(seed=42)
part = DistributionConfig(dist="truncated_normal", mean=10, std=2, low=0)
part.stream = "tasks.part.service_time"  # the sequence the blueprint draws from
failure = DistributionConfig(dist="exponential", rate=0.0033333333333333335)
failure.stream = "tasks.break_loop.wait.timeout"
repairman = simpy.PreemptiveResource(env, capacity=1)
names: dict = {}  # each machine's process, by the name its records carry
numbers = {task: itertools.count() for task in TASKS}

docs.title: Machine Works and Breaks
docs.text:
SimPy's Machine class makes parts in a loop. A second process, break_machine, interrupts the first after each failure time unless the machine is already broken. The interrupted machine asks for the repairman at priority 1, repairs, and goes on with the time it had left.

docs/snippets/simpy/machine_shop.py:machine-works-and-breaks
class Machine:
    """A machine produces parts and may get broken every now and then.

    If it breaks, it requests a *repairman* and continues the production
    after the it is repaired.

    A machine has a *name* and a number of *parts_made* thus far.

    """

    def __init__(self, env, name, repairman):
        self.env = env
        self.name = name
        self.parts_made = 0
        self.broken = False

        # Start "working" and "break_machine" processes for this machine.
        self.process = env.process(self.working(repairman))
        env.process(self.break_machine())

    def working(self, repairman):
        """Produce parts as long as the simulation runs.

        While making a part, the machine may break multiple times.
        Request a repairman when this happens.

        """
        while True:
            # Start making a new part
            done_in = time_per_part()
            while done_in:
                start = self.env.now
                try:
                    # Working on the part
                    yield self.env.timeout(done_in)
                    done_in = 0  # Set to 0 to exit while loop.

                except simpy.Interrupt:
                    self.broken = True
                    done_in -= self.env.now - start  # How much time left?

                    # Request a repairman. This will preempt its "other_job".
                    with repairman.request(priority=1) as req:
                        yield req
                        yield self.env.timeout(REPAIR_TIME)

                    self.broken = False

            # Part is done.
            self.parts_made += 1

    def break_machine(self):
        """Break the machine every now and then."""
        while True:
            yield self.env.timeout(time_to_failure())
            if not self.broken:
                # Only break the machine if it is currently working.
                self.process.interrupt()
YAMLBuilderLow-level

machines starts ten machines at time 0. start_machine starts each machine's break_loop and goes to part. part takes a truncated normal time and repeats with next: part. With on_interrupt: resume an interrupted part keeps the time it had left, and on_interrupt_run: begin_repair starts the repair. repair asks for the repairman at priority 1. break_loop waits an exponential time, and then interrupts the part of its machine, if that machine is not broken.

examples/low-level/simpy/machine_shop_example.py:machine-works-and-breaks
class Machine:
    """A machine that makes parts and breaks down now and then."""

    def __init__(self, name, number):
        self.name = name
        self.number = number
        self.broken = False
        self.process = env.process(self.working())
        names[self.process] = name

    def working(self):
        env.process(self.break_machine())
        started = {"event_type": "machine_started"}
        publish(self.name, "start_machine", next(numbers["start_machine"]), started)
        while True:
            making = next(numbers["part"])
            publish(self.name, "part", making, {"status": "started"})
            done_in = sampler.sample(part)
            while done_in:
                start = env.now
                try:
                    yield env.timeout(done_in)
                    done_in = 0
                except simpy.Interrupt:
                    interrupted = {"status": "interrupted", "cause": None}
                    publish(self.name, "part", making, interrupted)
                    broken = {"event_type": "broken"}
                    publish(
                        self.name,
                        "begin_repair",
                        next(numbers["begin_repair"]),
                        broken,
                    )
                    self.broken = True
                    done_in -= env.now - start
                    yield from self.repair()
                    publish(self.name, "part", making, {"status": "resumed"})
            publish(self.name, "part", making, {"event_type": "part_made"})

    def repair(self):
        number = next(numbers["repair"])
        publish(
            self.name,
            "repair",
            number,
            {"path_id": REPAIR, **REPAIR_NAMES, "status": "queued"},
        )
        # The repair goes before the repairman's other jobs
        with repairman.request(priority=1) as req:
            yield req
            publish(
                self.name,
                "repair",
                number,
                {"path_id": REPAIR, **REPAIR_NAMES, "status": "started"},
            )
            yield env.timeout(REPAIR_TIME)
        publish(self.name, "repair", number, {"event_type": "repaired"})
        self.broken = False

    def break_machine(self):
        name = f"break_loop-{self.number + 1}"
        while True:
            number = next(numbers["break_loop"])
            publish(name, "break_loop", number, {"status": "queued"})
            yield env.timeout(sampler.sample(failure))
            publish(name, "break_loop", number, {"status": "started"})
            publish(name, "break_loop", number, {"event_type": "tick"})
            if not self.broken:
                self.process.interrupt()

docs.title: Repairman Does Other Jobs
docs.text:
SimPy's other_jobs asks for the repairman at priority 2 and works on a 30 minute job. A repair preempts it, and the job resumes with the time it had left.

docs/snippets/simpy/machine_shop.py:repairman-other-jobs
def other_jobs(env, repairman):
    """The repairman's other (unimportant) job."""
    while True:
        # Start a new job
        done_in = JOB_DURATION
        while done_in:
            # Retry the job until it is done.
            # Its priority is lower than that of machine repairs.
            with repairman.request(priority=2) as req:
                yield req
                start = env.now
                try:
                    yield env.timeout(done_in)
                    done_in = 0
                except simpy.Interrupt:
                    done_in -= env.now - start

examples/low-level/simpy/machine_shop_example.py:repairman-other-jobs
def other_jobs(name):
    while True:
        number = next(numbers["other_job"])
        publish(name, "other_job", number, {"status": "queued"})
        done_in = JOB_DURATION
        status = "started"
        while done_in:
            with repairman.request(priority=2) as req:
                yield req
                publish(name, "other_job", number, {"status": status})
                start = env.now
                try:
                    yield env.timeout(done_in)
                    done_in = 0
                except simpy.Interrupt as interrupt:
                    preempted = interrupt.cause
                    publish(
                        name,
                        "other_job",
                        number,
                        {
                            "status": "preempted",
                            "resource": "repairman",
                            "preempted_by": names[preempted.by],
                            "usage_since": preempted.usage_since,
                        },
                    )
                    done_in -= env.now - start
                    status = "resumed"
        publish(name, "other_job", number, {"event_type": "other_done"})

docs.title: Check the Result
docs.text:
In the 40320 seconds the ten machines make 33906 parts. Machine 8 makes the most, 3494, and Machine 9 the fewest, 3284. In SimPy's output, below, the machines make between 3185 and 3387 parts each.

1040 machines break down and 1039 repairs finish, because the last repair is still running when the run ends. The repairman finishes 304 other jobs, and a repair preempts a job 269 times. SimPy's example does not print these counts. Here each one is a record with the machine's key, and the preempted job's record names the repair that preempted it. desflow draws each random value from its own stream, named by the place where the value is used, such as tasks.part.service_time. A seed of 42 therefore gives different numbers from SimPy's random.seed(42). The system is the same. The figures are not.

Machine 1 made 3273 parts.

Machine 3 made 3343 parts.

The three versions in desflow print the same records, which a test checks by running each version unpaced. Each record has sim_ts, the simulation time, and a key for the entity it belongs to. The statistics and the parameters that a live run can change are in the same stream, which SimPy's file does not have.

# Machine Shop: SimPy's machine_shop.py example, in YAML.
#
# The YAML version of machine_shop_example.py, which --api builder downloads. A shop
# has ten machines, each making parts without end; a part's time is normal with
# standard deviation 2, never below 0. Each machine breaks down after an exponential
# time, unless it is already broken. A broken machine waits for the one repairman, at
# priority 1, for its repair, and then finishes its part. Between repairs the
# repairman does other jobs at priority 2, which a repair preempts and which resume
# afterwards.
#
# SimPy's example counts minutes, and here each of its minutes is one second. So a
# part takes about 10 seconds, a machine breaks down about every 300 seconds, a repair
# and another job each take 30 seconds, and the run ends after 40320 seconds, SimPy's
# four weeks. Each value is drawn from desflow's random sequence for its place in the
# file, so the numbers differ from those SimPy prints.
#
# The breakdowns are written as tasks: each machine's `break_loop` waits for the
# next failure and interrupts the machine's `part`, whose `on_interrupt_run` starts the
# repair. `MachineShop.variables.parts_made` counts the parts of each machine.
#
# Needs no containers. Runs unpaced and ends after 40320 simulation seconds.
# Run it from its folder with: desflow run machine_shop.yaml

simulation: {sim_id: MachineShop, factor: 0, random_seed: 42}

egress:
  - {type: Console}

variables:
  target: -1
  parts_made: {}

resources:
  repairman: {current_cap: 1, queue: priority, preempt: true}

services:
  repair_time: {dist: constant, value: 30}

arrivals:
  machines:
    initial: 10
    spawn: start_machine
    key: {gen: sequence, format: "Machine {}"}
    attributes:
      id: {gen: sequence}
      parts_made: 0
      broken: 0
  others: {initial: 1, spawn: other_job}

tasks:
  start_machine:
    payload: {event_type: machine_started}
    spawn: {task: break_loop, copy_attributes: true}
    next: part
  part:
    service_time: {gen: sample, dist: truncated_normal, mean: 10, std: 2, low: 0}
    on_interrupt: resume
    on_interrupt_run: begin_repair
    set:
      parts_made: {gen: expr, expr: "attr.parts_made + 1"}
    on:
      - path: MachineShop.variables.parts_made
        value:
          gen: expr
          expr: "set_key(registry['MachineShop.variables.parts_made'], process.key,
            get_key(registry['MachineShop.variables.parts_made'], process.key, 0) + 1)"
    payload: {event_type: part_made}
    next: part
  begin_repair:
    payload: {event_type: broken}
    set: {broken: 1}
    next: repair
  repair:
    resource: repairman
    priority: 1
    service: repair_time
    set: {broken: 0}
    payload: {event_type: repaired}
  # The machine's failures: one wait for each, then an interrupt of its part
  break_loop:
    wait:
      timeout: {gen: sample, dist: exponential, rate: 0.0033333333333333335}
    payload: {event_type: tick}
    on:
      - path: MachineShop.variables.target
        value: {gen: expr, expr: "attr.id"}
      - interrupt:
          task: part
          where: "attr.id == registry['MachineShop.variables.target'] and attr.broken ==
            0"
    next: break_loop
  other_job:
    resource: repairman
    priority: 2
    service_time: 30
    on_interrupt: resume
    payload: {event_type: other_done}
    next: other_job

run: {until: 40320}

"""Machine Shop: SimPy's machine_shop.py example, builder API.

A shop has ten machines, each making parts without end; a part's time is normal with
standard deviation 2, never below 0. Each machine breaks down after an exponential
time, unless it is already broken. A broken machine waits for the one repairman, at
priority 1, for its repair, and then finishes its part. Between repairs the repairman
does other jobs at priority 2, which a repair preempts and which resume afterwards.

SimPy's example counts minutes, and here each of its minutes is one second. So a part
takes about 10 seconds, a machine breaks down about every 300 seconds, a repair and
another job each take 30 seconds, and the run ends after 40320 seconds, SimPy's four
weeks. Each value is drawn from desflow's random sequence for its place in the model,
so the numbers differ from those SimPy prints.

The breakdowns are written as tasks: each machine's `break_loop` waits for the next
failure and interrupts the machine's `part`, whose `on_interrupt_run` starts the
repair. `MachineShop.variables.parts_made` counts the parts of each machine.

Needs no containers. Runs unpaced and ends after 40320 simulation seconds.
"""

import logging

from desflow import ConsoleEgress, SimulationContext
from desflow.values import generator


def build(size: int = 10) -> SimulationContext:
    """Builds the shop, with `size` machines."""
    app = SimulationContext(sim_id="MachineShop", factor=0, random_seed=42)
    app.add_egress(ConsoleEgress())
    app.add_resource("repairman", current_cap=1, queue="priority", preempt=True)
    app.add_variable("target", -1)
    app.add_variable("parts_made", {})
    app.add_service("repair_time", dist="constant", value=30)
    app.add_initial_arrival(
        "machines",
        size,
        key=lambda n: "Machine {}".format(n - 1),
        attributes={"id": generator({"gen": "sequence"}), "parts_made": 0, "broken": 0},
        spawn="start_machine",
    )
    app.add_initial_arrival("others", 1, spawn="other_job")

    @app.task(
        name="start_machine",
        spawn={"task": "break_loop", "copy_attributes": True},
        next="part",
    )
    def start_machine(task_id):
        """Starts the machine and its failures."""
        return {"event_type": "machine_started"}

    @app.task(
        name="part",
        service_time=generator(
            {
                "gen": "sample",
                "dist": "truncated_normal",
                "mean": 10,
                "std": 2,
                "low": 0,
            }
        ),
        on_interrupt="resume",
        on_interrupt_run="begin_repair",
        set={"parts_made": generator({"gen": "expr", "expr": "attr.parts_made + 1"})},
        on=[
            {
                "path": "MachineShop.variables.parts_made",
                "value": generator(
                    {
                        "gen": "expr",
                        "expr": "set_key(registry['MachineShop.variables.parts_made'], process.key, get_key(registry['MachineShop.variables.parts_made'], process.key, 0) + 1)",
                    }
                ),
            }
        ],
        next="part",
    )
    def part(task_id):
        """Makes a part."""
        return {"event_type": "part_made"}

    @app.task(name="begin_repair", set={"broken": 1}, next="repair")
    def begin_repair(task_id):
        """Marks the machine broken."""
        return {"event_type": "broken"}

    @app.task(
        name="repair",
        resource_id="repairman",
        priority=1,
        service_id="repair_time",
        set={"broken": 0},
    )
    def repair(task_id):
        """Repairs the machine."""
        return {"event_type": "repaired"}

    # The machine's failures: one wait for each, then an interrupt of its part
    @app.task(
        name="break_loop",
        wait={
            "timeout": generator(
                {"gen": "sample", "dist": "exponential", "rate": 0.0033333333333333335}
            )
        },
        on=[
            {
                "path": "MachineShop.variables.target",
                "value": generator({"gen": "expr", "expr": "attr.id"}),
            },
            {
                "interrupt": {
                    "task": "part",
                    "where": "attr.id == registry['MachineShop.variables.target'] and attr.broken == 0",
                }
            },
        ],
        next="break_loop",
    )
    def break_loop(task_id):
        """Breaks the machine down."""
        return {"event_type": "tick"}


    @app.task(
        name="other_job",
        resource_id="repairman",
        priority=2,
        service_time=30,
        on_interrupt="resume",
        next="other_job",
    )
    def other_job(task_id):
        """Does one of the repairman's other jobs."""
        return {"event_type": "other_done"}


    return app


app = build()


def run(model: SimulationContext = app) -> None:
    """Runs 40320 seconds, SimPy's four weeks counted in minutes."""
    model.run(until=4 * 7 * 24 * 60)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    run()

examples/low-level/simpy/machine_shop_example.py
"""Machine Shop: SimPy's machine_shop.py example, low-level API.

The low-level version of `builder/simpy/machine_shop_example.py`: SimPy's own
`Machine` and `other_jobs` on a `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment`. They publish with
`publish_event` the records that the YAML and builder versions publish: each task's
`queued`, `started`, `interrupted`, `preempted` and `resumed`, its own events, and the
number of the task's instance. A shop has ten machines, each making parts without end.
Each machine breaks down now and then, unless it is already broken. A broken machine
waits for the one repairman, at priority 1, and then finishes its part. Between
repairs the repairman does other jobs at priority 2, which a repair preempts and which
resume afterwards.

SimPy's example counts minutes, and here each of its minutes is one second. So a part
takes about 10 seconds, a machine breaks down about every 300 seconds, a repair and
another job each take 30 seconds, and the run ends after 40320 seconds, SimPy's four
weeks. Each value is drawn from desflow's `Sampler`, from the random sequence the YAML
and builder versions use for the same place, so the three versions publish the same
records.

Needs no containers. Runs unpaced and ends after 40320 simulation seconds.
"""

import itertools
import logging

import simpy

from desflow import (
    ConsoleEgress,
    DistributionConfig,
    DynamicRealtimeEnvironment,
    Sampler,
)

REPAIR_TIME = 30
JOB_DURATION = 30
NUM_MACHINES = 10
UNTIL = 4 * 7 * 24 * 60  # SimPy's four weeks in minutes, read as seconds
REPAIR = "MachineShop.service.repair_time"  # the service a repair's records name
REPAIR_NAMES = {"sim_id": "MachineShop", "service": "repair_time"}
TASKS = ("start_machine", "part", "begin_repair", "repair", "break_loop", "other_job")


def build(env: DynamicRealtimeEnvironment, size: int = NUM_MACHINES) -> None:
    """Starts `size` machines and the repairman's other jobs on `env`."""
    sampler = Sampler(seed=42)
    part = DistributionConfig(dist="truncated_normal", mean=10, std=2, low=0)
    part.stream = "tasks.part.service_time"  # the sequence the blueprint draws from
    failure = DistributionConfig(dist="exponential", rate=0.0033333333333333335)
    failure.stream = "tasks.break_loop.wait.timeout"
    repairman = simpy.PreemptiveResource(env, capacity=1)
    names: dict = {}  # each machine's process, by the name its records carry
    numbers = {task: itertools.count() for task in TASKS}

    def publish(name, task, number, value):
        env.publish_event(name, value, task=task, instance=number)

    class Machine:
        """A machine that makes parts and breaks down now and then."""

        def __init__(self, name, number):
            self.name = name
            self.number = number
            self.broken = False
            self.process = env.process(self.working())
            names[self.process] = name

        def working(self):
            env.process(self.break_machine())
            started = {"event_type": "machine_started"}
            publish(self.name, "start_machine", next(numbers["start_machine"]), started)
            while True:
                making = next(numbers["part"])
                publish(self.name, "part", making, {"status": "started"})
                done_in = sampler.sample(part)
                while done_in:
                    start = env.now
                    try:
                        yield env.timeout(done_in)
                        done_in = 0
                    except simpy.Interrupt:
                        interrupted = {"status": "interrupted", "cause": None}
                        publish(self.name, "part", making, interrupted)
                        broken = {"event_type": "broken"}
                        publish(
                            self.name,
                            "begin_repair",
                            next(numbers["begin_repair"]),
                            broken,
                        )
                        self.broken = True
                        done_in -= env.now - start
                        yield from self.repair()
                        publish(self.name, "part", making, {"status": "resumed"})
                publish(self.name, "part", making, {"event_type": "part_made"})

        def repair(self):
            number = next(numbers["repair"])
            publish(
                self.name,
                "repair",
                number,
                {"path_id": REPAIR, **REPAIR_NAMES, "status": "queued"},
            )
            # The repair goes before the repairman's other jobs
            with repairman.request(priority=1) as req:
                yield req
                publish(
                    self.name,
                    "repair",
                    number,
                    {"path_id": REPAIR, **REPAIR_NAMES, "status": "started"},
                )
                yield env.timeout(REPAIR_TIME)
            publish(self.name, "repair", number, {"event_type": "repaired"})
            self.broken = False

        def break_machine(self):
            name = f"break_loop-{self.number + 1}"
            while True:
                number = next(numbers["break_loop"])
                publish(name, "break_loop", number, {"status": "queued"})
                yield env.timeout(sampler.sample(failure))
                publish(name, "break_loop", number, {"status": "started"})
                publish(name, "break_loop", number, {"event_type": "tick"})
                if not self.broken:
                    self.process.interrupt()


    def other_jobs(name):
        while True:
            number = next(numbers["other_job"])
            publish(name, "other_job", number, {"status": "queued"})
            done_in = JOB_DURATION
            status = "started"
            while done_in:
                with repairman.request(priority=2) as req:
                    yield req
                    publish(name, "other_job", number, {"status": status})
                    start = env.now
                    try:
                        yield env.timeout(done_in)
                        done_in = 0
                    except simpy.Interrupt as interrupt:
                        preempted = interrupt.cause
                        publish(
                            name,
                            "other_job",
                            number,
                            {
                                "status": "preempted",
                                "resource": "repairman",
                                "preempted_by": names[preempted.by],
                                "usage_since": preempted.usage_since,
                            },
                        )
                        done_in -= env.now - start
                        status = "resumed"
            publish(name, "other_job", number, {"event_type": "other_done"})


    for number in range(size):
        Machine(f"Machine {number}", number)
    env.process(other_jobs("others-1"))


def run() -> None:
    """Runs 40320 seconds, SimPy's four weeks counted in minutes."""
    env = DynamicRealtimeEnvironment(factor=0)
    env.setup_egress([ConsoleEgress()])
    build(env)
    try:
        env.run(until=UNTIL)
    finally:
        env.teardown()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    run()

"""
Machine shop example

Covers:

- Interrupts
- Resources: PreemptiveResource

Scenario:
  A workshop has *n* identical machines. A stream of jobs (enough to
  keep the machines busy) arrives. Each machine breaks down
  periodically. Repairs are carried out by one repairman. The repairman
  has other, less important tasks to perform, too. Broken machines
  preempt these tasks. The repairman continues them when he is done
  with the machine repair. The workshop works continuously.

"""

import random

import simpy

# fmt: off
RANDOM_SEED = 42
PT_MEAN = 10.0         # Avg. processing time in minutes
PT_SIGMA = 2.0         # Sigma of processing time
MTTF = 300.0           # Mean time to failure in minutes
BREAK_MEAN = 1 / MTTF  # Param. for expovariate distribution
REPAIR_TIME = 30.0     # Time it takes to repair a machine in minutes
JOB_DURATION = 30.0    # Duration of other jobs in minutes
NUM_MACHINES = 10      # Number of machines in the machine shop
WEEKS = 4              # Simulation time in weeks
SIM_TIME = WEEKS * 7 * 24 * 60  # Simulation time in minutes
# fmt: on


def time_per_part():
    """Return actual processing time for a concrete part."""
    t = random.normalvariate(PT_MEAN, PT_SIGMA)
    # The normalvariate can be negative, but we want only positive times.
    while t <= 0:
        t = random.normalvariate(PT_MEAN, PT_SIGMA)
    return t


def time_to_failure():
    """Return time until next failure for a machine."""
    return random.expovariate(BREAK_MEAN)


class Machine:
    """A machine produces parts and may get broken every now and then.

    If it breaks, it requests a *repairman* and continues the production
    after the it is repaired.

    A machine has a *name* and a number of *parts_made* thus far.

    """

    def __init__(self, env, name, repairman):
        self.env = env
        self.name = name
        self.parts_made = 0
        self.broken = False

        # Start "working" and "break_machine" processes for this machine.
        self.process = env.process(self.working(repairman))
        env.process(self.break_machine())

    def working(self, repairman):
        """Produce parts as long as the simulation runs.

        While making a part, the machine may break multiple times.
        Request a repairman when this happens.

        """
        while True:
            # Start making a new part
            done_in = time_per_part()
            while done_in:
                start = self.env.now
                try:
                    # Working on the part
                    yield self.env.timeout(done_in)
                    done_in = 0  # Set to 0 to exit while loop.

                except simpy.Interrupt:
                    self.broken = True
                    done_in -= self.env.now - start  # How much time left?

                    # Request a repairman. This will preempt its "other_job".
                    with repairman.request(priority=1) as req:
                        yield req
                        yield self.env.timeout(REPAIR_TIME)

                    self.broken = False

            # Part is done.
            self.parts_made += 1

    def break_machine(self):
        """Break the machine every now and then."""
        while True:
            yield self.env.timeout(time_to_failure())
            if not self.broken:
                # Only break the machine if it is currently working.
                self.process.interrupt()


def other_jobs(env, repairman):
    """The repairman's other (unimportant) job."""
    while True:
        # Start a new job
        done_in = JOB_DURATION
        while done_in:
            # Retry the job until it is done.
            # Its priority is lower than that of machine repairs.
            with repairman.request(priority=2) as req:
                yield req
                start = env.now
                try:
                    yield env.timeout(done_in)
                    done_in = 0
                except simpy.Interrupt:
                    done_in -= env.now - start


# Setup and start the simulation
print('Machine shop')
random.seed(RANDOM_SEED)  # This helps to reproduce the results

# Create an environment and start the setup process
env = simpy.Environment()
repairman = simpy.PreemptiveResource(env, capacity=1)
machines = [Machine(env, f'Machine {i}', repairman) for i in range(NUM_MACHINES)]
env.process(other_jobs(env, repairman))

# Execute!
env.run(until=SIM_TIME)

# Analysis/results
print(f'Machine shop results after {WEEKS} weeks')
for machine in machines:
    print(f'{machine.name} made {machine.parts_made} parts.')

docs.title: Movie Renege
docs.text: A ticket counter sells tickets for three films, and a film that sells out sends its queue away. This is SimPy's Movie Renege example, written in desflow.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
SimPy's theatre has one ticket counter and three films with 50 tickets each. A moviegoer arrives about every 0.5 minutes (exponential gaps), picks a film and 1 to 6 tickets, and joins the queue only while the film has tickets. At the counter, a moviegoer who asks for more tickets than are left argues for 0.5 minutes and leaves. Otherwise the sale takes 1 minute. When fewer than 2 tickets are left, the film is sold out and everyone still queueing for it leaves (reneges). The run lasts 120 minutes. desflow reads each of SimPy's minutes as one second.

The example needs only desflow, which each Quick Start in Run It installs, and no other service. desflow examples get simpy-movie-renege --api yaml downloads it, as Get an Example shows. SimPy Examples says how these pages read SimPy's times and numbers. SimPy's own page for the example is on its documentation site.

docs.title: Theater
docs.text:
SimPy's theater holds the counter, the tickets left for each film, the time each film sold out and the number of moviegoers who left each queue.

docs/snippets/simpy/movie_renege.py:theater
class Theater(NamedTuple):
    counter: simpy.Resource
    movies: List[str]
    available: Dict[str, int]
    sold_out: Dict[str, simpy.Event]
    when_sold_out: Dict[str, Optional[float]]
    num_renegers: Dict[str, int]
YAMLBuilderLow-level

available, when_sold_out and num_renegers are variables that hold one number for each film. counter is a resource with one unit. sold_out is a signal family with one member for each film, and once: true makes a member fire one time.

examples/yaml/simpy/movie_renege.yaml:theater
variables:
  available: {Python Unchained: 50, Kill Process: 50, Pulp Implementation: 50}
  when_sold_out: {}
  num_renegers: {Python Unchained: 0, Kill Process: 0, Pulp Implementation: 0}

resources:
  counter: {current_cap: 1}

signals:
  sold_out: {family: true, once: true}

add_resource, add_variable and add_signal declare the same parts.

examples/builder/simpy/movie_renege_example.py:theater
app.add_resource("counter", current_cap=1)
app.add_variable("available", {movie: 50 for movie in MOVIES})
app.add_variable("when_sold_out", {})
app.add_variable("num_renegers", {movie: 0 for movie in MOVIES})
app.add_signal("sold_out", family=True, once=True)

The low-level version has SimPy's simpy.Resource for the counter, a dictionary for the tickets left and one env.event() for each film.

examples/low-level/simpy/movie_renege_example.py:theater
counter = simpy.Resource(env, capacity=1)
available = {movie: TICKETS for movie in MOVIES}
sold_out = {movie: env.event() for movie in MOVIES}
numbers = {task: itertools.count() for task in TASKS}

docs.title: Moviegoers Arrive
docs.text:
SimPy's customer_arrivals starts a moviegoer after each exponential gap, with a random film and a number of tickets.

docs/snippets/simpy/movie_renege.py:moviegoers-arrive
def customer_arrivals(env, theater):
    """Create new *moviegoers* until the sim time reaches 120."""
    while True:
        yield env.timeout(random.expovariate(1 / 0.5))

        movie = random.choice(theater.movies)
        num_tickets = random.randint(1, 6)
        if theater.available[movie]:
            env.process(moviegoer(env, movie, num_tickets, theater))
YAMLBuilderLow-level

The arrival goers has exponential gaps at the rate 2 a second. Each moviegoer has two attributes: movie, one of the three films, and tickets, an integer from 1 to 6.

examples/yaml/simpy/movie_renege.yaml:moviegoers-arrive
arrivals:
  goers:
    dist: exponential
    rate: 2
    spawn: moviegoer
    attributes:
      movie:
        gen: one_of
        choices: [Python Unchained, Kill Process, Pulp Implementation]
      tickets: {gen: integer, bounds: [1, 6]}

add_arrival takes the same attributes, written as generators.

examples/builder/simpy/movie_renege_example.py:moviegoers-arrive
app.add_arrival(
    "goers",
    "exponential",
    rate=2,
    attributes={
        "movie": generator({"gen": "one_of", "choices": MOVIES}),
        "tickets": generator({"gen": "integer", "bounds": [1, 6]}),
    },
    spawn="moviegoer",
)

customer_arrivals is SimPy's function. It draws the gap, the film and the number of tickets from desflow's Sampler.

examples/low-level/simpy/movie_renege_example.py:moviegoers-arrive

        movie = MOVIES[int(movie_choices.integers(len(MOVIES)))]
        num_tickets = int(ticket_counts.integers(1, 7))

env.process(customer_arrivals())

docs.title: Moviegoer Waits or Leaves
docs.text:
SimPy's moviegoer requests the counter. It waits for either its turn or the film to sell out. If the film sells out first, the moviegoer leaves.

docs/snippets/simpy/movie_renege.py:moviegoer-buys-or-leaves
def moviegoer(env, movie, num_tickets, theater):
    """A moviegoer tries to by a number of tickets (*num_tickets*) for
    a certain *movie* in a *theater*.

    If the movie becomes sold out, she leaves the theater. If she gets
    to the counter, she tries to buy a number of tickets. If not enough
    tickets are left, she argues with the teller and leaves.

    If at most one ticket is left after the moviegoer bought her
    tickets, the *sold out* event for this movie is triggered causing
    all remaining moviegoers to leave.

    """
    with theater.counter.request() as my_turn:
        # Wait until it's our turn or until the movie is sold out
        result = yield my_turn | theater.sold_out[movie]

        # Check if it's our turn or if movie is sold out
        if my_turn not in result:
            theater.num_renegers[movie] += 1
            return

        # Check if enough tickets left.
        if theater.available[movie] < num_tickets:
            # Moviegoer leaves after some discussion
            yield env.timeout(0.5)
            return

        # Buy tickets
        theater.available[movie] -= num_tickets
        if theater.available[movie] < SELLOUT_THRESHOLD:
            # Trigger the "sold out" event for the movie
            theater.sold_out[movie].succeed()
            theater.when_sold_out[movie] = env.now
            theater.available[movie] = 0
        yield env.timeout(1)
YAMLBuilderLow-level

balk stops a moviegoer from joining when the film has no tickets left. open places a request for the counter and calls it slot, and wait: any waits for the turn or for the sold_out signal of the moviegoer's film, whichever comes first. If the turn came first the moviegoer goes to serve. Otherwise it goes to leave, which cancels the request and counts a moviegoer who reneged.

examples/yaml/simpy/movie_renege.yaml:moviegoer-waits
moviegoer:
  balk: "registry['Movie.variables.available'][attr.movie] == 0"
  open:
    slot: {request: counter}
  wait:
    any:
      turn: {handle: slot}
      out:
        signal: {of: sold_out, key: "attr.movie"}
  payload: {event_type: at_counter}
  next:
    when:
      - {condition: "wait.turn.done", task: serve}
    default: leave
leave:
  cancel: slot
  release: {handle: slot}
  payload:
    event_type: reneged
    movie: {gen: expr, expr: attr.movie}
  on:
    - path: Movie.variables.num_renegers
      value:
        gen: expr
        expr: "set_key(registry['Movie.variables.num_renegers'], attr.movie,
          get_key(registry['Movie.variables.num_renegers'], attr.movie, 0) + 1)"

The same two tasks, with open, wait and next as in the YAML.

examples/builder/simpy/movie_renege_example.py:moviegoer-waits
@app.task(
    name="moviegoer",
    balk="registry['Movie.variables.available'][attr.movie] == 0",
    open={"slot": {"request": "counter"}},
    wait={
        "any": {
            "turn": {"handle": "slot"},
            "out": {"signal": {"of": "sold_out", "key": "attr.movie"}},
        }
    },
    next={
        "when": [{"condition": "wait.turn.done", "task": "serve"}],
        "default": "leave",
    },
)
def moviegoer(task_id):
    """Waits for the counter or for the movie to sell out."""
    return {"event_type": "at_counter"}

leave_payload = Template(
    {"event_type": "reneged", "movie": {"gen": "expr", "expr": "attr.movie"}},
    name="leave",
)

@app.task(
    name="leave",
    cancel="slot",
    release={"handle": "slot"},
    on=[
        {
            "path": "Movie.variables.num_renegers",
            "value": generator(
                {
                    "gen": "expr",
                    "expr": "set_key(registry['Movie.variables.num_renegers'], attr.movie, get_key(registry['Movie.variables.num_renegers'], attr.movie, 0) + 1)",
                }
            ),
        }
    ],
)
def leave(task_id):
    """Leaves the queue: the movie sold out."""
    return leave_payload

moviegoer is SimPy's function, with turn | sold_out[movie]. This block shows its first part, up to the moviegoer who leaves.

examples/low-level/simpy/movie_renege_example.py:moviegoer-waits
def moviegoer(name, movie, num_tickets):
    number = next(numbers["moviegoer"])

    def publish(task, value, instance=None):
        """Publishes `value` as `instance` of `task`, or as a new instance."""
        step = next(numbers[task]) if instance is None else instance
        env.publish_event(name, value, task=task, instance=step)
        return step

    if available[movie] == 0:  # sold out: does not join the queue
        publish("moviegoer", {"status": "balked"}, number)
        return
    # The task's wait and the counter's request it opens each publish queued
    publish("moviegoer", {"status": "queued"}, number)
    publish("moviegoer", {"status": "queued"}, number)
    turn = counter.request()
    result = yield turn | sold_out[movie]
    if turn in result:  # the request publishes started as it is granted
        publish("moviegoer", {"status": "started"}, number)
    publish("moviegoer", {"status": "started"}, number)
    publish("moviegoer", {"event_type": "at_counter"}, number)
    if turn not in result:  # the movie sold out while it queued
        turn.cancel()
        if turn.triggered:
            counter.release(turn)
        publish("leave", {"event_type": "reneged", "movie": movie})
        return

docs.title: Counter Sells or Argues
docs.text:
At the counter SimPy's moviegoer checks the tickets left. A moviegoer who asks for too many argues and leaves. Otherwise the tickets are bought, and the film is sold out when fewer than 2 are left.

YAMLBuilderLow-level

serve goes to argue when the film has fewer tickets left than the moviegoer asks for. argue takes 0.5 seconds and releases the counter. Otherwise buy takes the tickets from available, and check goes to sold when fewer than 2 are left.

examples/yaml/simpy/movie_renege.yaml:counter-sells
serve:
  payload: {event_type: served}
  next:
    when:
      - condition: "registry['Movie.variables.available'][attr.movie] < attr.tickets"
        task: argue
    default: buy
argue:
  service_time: 0.5
  payload: {event_type: argued}
  release: {handle: slot}
buy:
  payload: {event_type: bought}
  on:
    - path: Movie.variables.available
      value:
        gen: expr
        expr: "set_key(registry['Movie.variables.available'], attr.movie,
          registry['Movie.variables.available'][attr.movie] - attr.tickets)"
  next: check
check:
  payload: {event_type: checked}
  next:
    when:
      - condition: "registry['Movie.variables.available'][attr.movie] < 2"
        task: sold
    default: finish

The tasks serve, argue, buy and check, with the same rules.

examples/builder/simpy/movie_renege_example.py:counter-sells
@app.task(
    name="serve",
    next={
        "when": [
            {
                "condition": "registry['Movie.variables.available'][attr.movie] < attr.tickets",
                "task": "argue",
            }
        ],
        "default": "buy",
    },
)
def serve(task_id):
    """Reaches the counter."""
    return {"event_type": "served"}

@app.task(name="argue", service_time=0.5, release={"handle": "slot"})
def argue(task_id):
    """Asks for more tickets than are left."""
    return {"event_type": "argued"}

@app.task(
    name="buy",
    on=[
        {
            "path": "Movie.variables.available",
            "value": generator(
                {
                    "gen": "expr",
                    "expr": "set_key(registry['Movie.variables.available'], attr.movie, registry['Movie.variables.available'][attr.movie] - attr.tickets)",
                }
            ),
        }
    ],
    next="check",
)
def buy(task_id):
    """Buys the tickets."""
    return {"event_type": "bought"}

@app.task(
    name="check",
    next={
        "when": [
            {
                "condition": "registry['Movie.variables.available'][attr.movie] < 2",
                "task": "sold",
            }
        ],
        "default": "finish",
    },
)
def check(task_id):
    """Checks how many tickets are left."""
    return {"event_type": "checked"}

The middle of the same moviegoer function.

examples/low-level/simpy/movie_renege_example.py:counter-sells
publish("serve", {"event_type": "served"})
if available[movie] < num_tickets:
    arguing = publish("argue", {"status": "started"})
    yield env.timeout(0.5)
    publish("argue", {"event_type": "argued"}, arguing)
    counter.release(turn)
    return
publish("buy", {"event_type": "bought"})
available[movie] -= num_tickets
publish("check", {"event_type": "checked"})

docs.title: Film Sells Out
docs.text:
When a film is sold out, SimPy's moviegoer fires the film's event, which sends the queue away, and records the time. The sale takes 1 minute and the counter is released.

YAMLBuilderLow-level

sold fires the sold_out signal of the film, which ends the wait of everyone queueing for it. It also records the time and sets the tickets left to 0, so later moviegoers balk. finish takes 1 second and releases the counter.

examples/yaml/simpy/movie_renege.yaml:film-sells-out
sold:
  payload:
    event_type: sold_out
    movie: {gen: expr, expr: attr.movie}
  on:
    - fire:
        signal: {of: sold_out, key: "attr.movie"}
    - path: Movie.variables.when_sold_out
      value:
        gen: expr
        expr: "set_key(registry['Movie.variables.when_sold_out'], attr.movie, t)"
    - path: Movie.variables.available
      value:
        gen: expr
        expr: "set_key(registry['Movie.variables.available'], attr.movie, 0)"
  next: finish
finish:
  service_time: 1
  payload: {event_type: done}
  release: {handle: slot}

The tasks sold and finish, with the same rules.

examples/builder/simpy/movie_renege_example.py:film-sells-out
sold_payload = Template(
    {"event_type": "sold_out", "movie": {"gen": "expr", "expr": "attr.movie"}},
    name="sold",
)

@app.task(
    name="sold",
    on=[
        {"fire": {"signal": {"of": "sold_out", "key": "attr.movie"}}},
        {
            "path": "Movie.variables.when_sold_out",
            "value": generator(
                {
                    "gen": "expr",
                    "expr": "set_key(registry['Movie.variables.when_sold_out'], attr.movie, t)",
                }
            ),
        },
        {
            "path": "Movie.variables.available",
            "value": generator(
                {
                    "gen": "expr",
                    "expr": "set_key(registry['Movie.variables.available'], attr.movie, 0)",
                }
            ),
        },
    ],
    next="finish",
)
def sold(task_id):
    """Sells the movie out, which sends its queue away."""
    return sold_payload

@app.task(name="finish", service_time=1, release={"handle": "slot"})
def finish(task_id):
    """Finishes the sale."""
    return {"event_type": "done"}

The end of the same moviegoer function.

examples/low-level/simpy/movie_renege_example.py:film-sells-out
if available[movie] < 2:
    publish("sold", {"event_type": "sold_out", "movie": movie})
    sold_out[movie].succeed()
    available[movie] = 0
finishing = publish("finish", {"status": "started"})
yield env.timeout(1)
publish("finish", {"event_type": "done"}, finishing)
counter.release(turn)

docs.text:
Pulp Implementation sells out at 21.793 seconds, Kill Process at 41.793 seconds and Python Unchained at 44.293 seconds. 18 moviegoers leave the queue for Python Unchained, 17 for Kill Process and 9 for Pulp Implementation. 44 sales go through, and 197 moviegoers find their film sold out and do not join a queue.

SimPy's output, below, has the films selling out at 38, 43 and 28 minutes, with 16, 5 and 5 moviegoers leaving. SimPy prints no count of moviegoers who find a film sold out. Here each one has a balked record. desflow draws each random value from its own stream, named by the place where the value is used, such as arrivals.goers.attributes.tickets. A seed of 42 therefore gives different numbers from SimPy's random.seed(42). The system is the same. The figures are not.

# Movie Renege: SimPy's movie_renege.py example, in YAML.
#
# The YAML version of movie_renege_example.py, which --api builder downloads. A movie
# theatre has one ticket counter and three movies with 50 tickets each. A moviegoer
# arrives at exponential gaps, picks a movie and 1 to 6 tickets, and does not join the
# queue once the movie is sold out. At the counter, a moviegoer who asks for more
# tickets than are left argues and leaves; otherwise the sale goes ahead. When fewer
# than 2 tickets are left the movie is sold out, and everyone still queueing for it
# leaves (reneged).
#
# SimPy's example counts minutes, and here each of its minutes is one second. So a
# moviegoer arrives about every 0.5 seconds, an argument takes 0.5 seconds, a sale 1
# second, and the run ends after 120 seconds, SimPy's 120 minutes. Each value is drawn
# from desflow's random sequence for its place in the file, so the numbers differ from
# those SimPy prints.
#
# The counter is a request opened by the moviegoer and held across the tasks that
# follow, and each movie's sold-out event is one member of the signal family
# `sold_out`.
#
# Needs no containers. Runs unpaced and ends after 120 simulation seconds.
# Run it from its folder with: desflow run movie_renege.yaml

simulation: {sim_id: Movie, factor: 0, random_seed: 42}

egress:
  - {type: Console}

variables:
  available: {Python Unchained: 50, Kill Process: 50, Pulp Implementation: 50}
  when_sold_out: {}
  num_renegers: {Python Unchained: 0, Kill Process: 0, Pulp Implementation: 0}

resources:
  counter: {current_cap: 1}

signals:
  sold_out: {family: true, once: true}

arrivals:
  goers:
    dist: exponential
    rate: 2
    spawn: moviegoer
    attributes:
      movie:
        gen: one_of
        choices: [Python Unchained, Kill Process, Pulp Implementation]
      tickets: {gen: integer, bounds: [1, 6]}

tasks:
  moviegoer:
    balk: "registry['Movie.variables.available'][attr.movie] == 0"
    open:
      slot: {request: counter}
    wait:
      any:
        turn: {handle: slot}
        out:
          signal: {of: sold_out, key: "attr.movie"}
    payload: {event_type: at_counter}
    next:
      when:
        - {condition: "wait.turn.done", task: serve}
      default: leave
  leave:
    cancel: slot
    release: {handle: slot}
    payload:
      event_type: reneged
      movie: {gen: expr, expr: attr.movie}
    on:
      - path: Movie.variables.num_renegers
        value:
          gen: expr
          expr: "set_key(registry['Movie.variables.num_renegers'], attr.movie,
            get_key(registry['Movie.variables.num_renegers'], attr.movie, 0) + 1)"
  serve:
    payload: {event_type: served}
    next:
      when:
        - condition: "registry['Movie.variables.available'][attr.movie] < attr.tickets"
          task: argue
      default: buy
  argue:
    service_time: 0.5
    payload: {event_type: argued}
    release: {handle: slot}
  buy:
    payload: {event_type: bought}
    on:
      - path: Movie.variables.available
        value:
          gen: expr
          expr: "set_key(registry['Movie.variables.available'], attr.movie,
            registry['Movie.variables.available'][attr.movie] - attr.tickets)"
    next: check
  check:
    payload: {event_type: checked}
    next:
      when:
        - condition: "registry['Movie.variables.available'][attr.movie] < 2"
          task: sold
      default: finish
  sold:
    payload:
      event_type: sold_out
      movie: {gen: expr, expr: attr.movie}
    on:
      - fire:
          signal: {of: sold_out, key: "attr.movie"}
      - path: Movie.variables.when_sold_out
        value:
          gen: expr
          expr: "set_key(registry['Movie.variables.when_sold_out'], attr.movie, t)"
      - path: Movie.variables.available
        value:
          gen: expr
          expr: "set_key(registry['Movie.variables.available'], attr.movie, 0)"
    next: finish
  finish:
    service_time: 1
    payload: {event_type: done}
    release: {handle: slot}

run: {until: 120}

examples/builder/simpy/movie_renege_example.py
"""Movie Renege: SimPy's movie_renege.py example, builder API.

A movie theatre has one ticket counter and three movies with 50 tickets each. A
moviegoer arrives at exponential gaps, picks a movie and 1 to 6 tickets, and does not
join the queue once the movie is sold out. At the counter, a moviegoer who asks for
more tickets than are left argues and leaves; otherwise the sale goes ahead. When fewer
than 2 tickets are left the movie is sold out, and everyone still queueing for it
leaves (reneged).

SimPy's example counts minutes, and here each of its minutes is one second. So a
moviegoer arrives about every 0.5 seconds, an argument takes 0.5 seconds, a sale 1
second, and the run ends after 120 seconds, SimPy's 120 minutes. Each value is drawn
from desflow's random sequence for its place in the model, so the numbers differ from
those SimPy prints.

The counter is a request opened by the moviegoer and held across the tasks that
follow, and each movie's sold-out event is one member of the signal family `sold_out`.

Needs no containers. Runs unpaced and ends after 120 simulation seconds.
"""

import logging

from desflow import ConsoleEgress, SimulationContext
from desflow.values import Template, generator

MOVIES = ["Python Unchained", "Kill Process", "Pulp Implementation"]


def build() -> SimulationContext:
    """Builds the theatre."""
    app = SimulationContext(sim_id="Movie", factor=0, random_seed=42)
    app.add_egress(ConsoleEgress())
    app.add_resource("counter", current_cap=1)
    app.add_variable("available", {movie: 50 for movie in MOVIES})
    app.add_variable("when_sold_out", {})
    app.add_variable("num_renegers", {movie: 0 for movie in MOVIES})
    app.add_signal("sold_out", family=True, once=True)
    app.add_arrival(
        "goers",
        "exponential",
        rate=2,
        attributes={
            "movie": generator({"gen": "one_of", "choices": MOVIES}),
            "tickets": generator({"gen": "integer", "bounds": [1, 6]}),
        },
        spawn="moviegoer",
    )

    @app.task(
        name="moviegoer",
        balk="registry['Movie.variables.available'][attr.movie] == 0",
        open={"slot": {"request": "counter"}},
        wait={
            "any": {
                "turn": {"handle": "slot"},
                "out": {"signal": {"of": "sold_out", "key": "attr.movie"}},
            }
        },
        next={
            "when": [{"condition": "wait.turn.done", "task": "serve"}],
            "default": "leave",
        },
    )
    def moviegoer(task_id):
        """Waits for the counter or for the movie to sell out."""
        return {"event_type": "at_counter"}

    leave_payload = Template(
        {"event_type": "reneged", "movie": {"gen": "expr", "expr": "attr.movie"}},
        name="leave",
    )

    @app.task(
        name="leave",
        cancel="slot",
        release={"handle": "slot"},
        on=[
            {
                "path": "Movie.variables.num_renegers",
                "value": generator(
                    {
                        "gen": "expr",
                        "expr": "set_key(registry['Movie.variables.num_renegers'], attr.movie, get_key(registry['Movie.variables.num_renegers'], attr.movie, 0) + 1)",
                    }
                ),
            }
        ],
    )
    def leave(task_id):
        """Leaves the queue: the movie sold out."""
        return leave_payload


    @app.task(
        name="serve",
        next={
            "when": [
                {
                    "condition": "registry['Movie.variables.available'][attr.movie] < attr.tickets",
                    "task": "argue",
                }
            ],
            "default": "buy",
        },
    )
    def serve(task_id):
        """Reaches the counter."""
        return {"event_type": "served"}

    @app.task(name="argue", service_time=0.5, release={"handle": "slot"})
    def argue(task_id):
        """Asks for more tickets than are left."""
        return {"event_type": "argued"}

    @app.task(
        name="buy",
        on=[
            {
                "path": "Movie.variables.available",
                "value": generator(
                    {
                        "gen": "expr",
                        "expr": "set_key(registry['Movie.variables.available'], attr.movie, registry['Movie.variables.available'][attr.movie] - attr.tickets)",
                    }
                ),
            }
        ],
        next="check",
    )
    def buy(task_id):
        """Buys the tickets."""
        return {"event_type": "bought"}

    @app.task(
        name="check",
        next={
            "when": [
                {
                    "condition": "registry['Movie.variables.available'][attr.movie] < 2",
                    "task": "sold",
                }
            ],
            "default": "finish",
        },
    )
    def check(task_id):
        """Checks how many tickets are left."""
        return {"event_type": "checked"}


    sold_payload = Template(
        {"event_type": "sold_out", "movie": {"gen": "expr", "expr": "attr.movie"}},
        name="sold",
    )

    @app.task(
        name="sold",
        on=[
            {"fire": {"signal": {"of": "sold_out", "key": "attr.movie"}}},
            {
                "path": "Movie.variables.when_sold_out",
                "value": generator(
                    {
                        "gen": "expr",
                        "expr": "set_key(registry['Movie.variables.when_sold_out'], attr.movie, t)",
                    }
                ),
            },
            {
                "path": "Movie.variables.available",
                "value": generator(
                    {
                        "gen": "expr",
                        "expr": "set_key(registry['Movie.variables.available'], attr.movie, 0)",
                    }
                ),
            },
        ],
        next="finish",
    )
    def sold(task_id):
        """Sells the movie out, which sends its queue away."""
        return sold_payload

    @app.task(name="finish", service_time=1, release={"handle": "slot"})
    def finish(task_id):
        """Finishes the sale."""
        return {"event_type": "done"}


    return app


app = build()


def run(model: SimulationContext = app) -> None:
    """Runs 120 simulation seconds."""
    model.run(until=120)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    run()

examples/low-level/simpy/movie_renege_example.py
"""Movie Renege: SimPy's movie_renege.py example, low-level API.

The low-level version of `builder/simpy/movie_renege_example.py`: SimPy's own
`moviegoer` and `customer_arrivals` on a `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment`. They publish
with `publish_event` the records that the YAML and builder versions publish: each
task's `queued`, `started` and `balked`, its own events, and the number of the task's
instance. A movie theatre has one ticket counter and three movies with 50 tickets
each. A moviegoer picks a movie and 1 to 6 tickets, and does not join the queue once
the movie is sold out. At the counter, a moviegoer who asks for more tickets than are
left argues and leaves; otherwise the sale goes ahead. When fewer than 2 tickets are
left the movie is sold out, and everyone still queueing for it leaves.

SimPy's example counts minutes, and here each of its minutes is one second. So a
moviegoer arrives about every 0.5 seconds, an argument takes 0.5 seconds, a sale 1
second, and the run ends after 120 seconds, SimPy's 120 minutes. Each value is drawn
from desflow's `Sampler`, from the random sequence the YAML and builder versions use
for the same place, so the three versions publish the same records.

Needs no containers. Runs unpaced and ends after 120 simulation seconds.
"""

import itertools
import logging

import simpy

from desflow import (
    ConsoleEgress,
    DistributionConfig,
    DynamicRealtimeEnvironment,
    Sampler,
)

MOVIES = ["Python Unchained", "Kill Process", "Pulp Implementation"]
TICKETS = 50
UNTIL = 120
TASKS = ("moviegoer", "leave", "serve", "argue", "buy", "check", "sold", "finish")


def build(env: DynamicRealtimeEnvironment) -> None:
    """Starts the moviegoers' arrivals on `env`."""
    sampler = Sampler(seed=42)
    gap = DistributionConfig(dist="exponential", rate=2)
    gap.stream = "arrival.goers"  # the sequence the blueprint's arrival draws from
    movie_choices = sampler.generator("arrivals.goers.attributes.movie")
    ticket_counts = sampler.generator("arrivals.goers.attributes.tickets")
    counter = simpy.Resource(env, capacity=1)
    available = {movie: TICKETS for movie in MOVIES}
    sold_out = {movie: env.event() for movie in MOVIES}
    numbers = {task: itertools.count() for task in TASKS}

    def moviegoer(name, movie, num_tickets):
        number = next(numbers["moviegoer"])

        def publish(task, value, instance=None):
            """Publishes `value` as `instance` of `task`, or as a new instance."""
            step = next(numbers[task]) if instance is None else instance
            env.publish_event(name, value, task=task, instance=step)
            return step

        if available[movie] == 0:  # sold out: does not join the queue
            publish("moviegoer", {"status": "balked"}, number)
            return
        # The task's wait and the counter's request it opens each publish queued
        publish("moviegoer", {"status": "queued"}, number)
        publish("moviegoer", {"status": "queued"}, number)
        turn = counter.request()
        result = yield turn | sold_out[movie]
        if turn in result:  # the request publishes started as it is granted
            publish("moviegoer", {"status": "started"}, number)
        publish("moviegoer", {"status": "started"}, number)
        publish("moviegoer", {"event_type": "at_counter"}, number)
        if turn not in result:  # the movie sold out while it queued
            turn.cancel()
            if turn.triggered:
                counter.release(turn)
            publish("leave", {"event_type": "reneged", "movie": movie})
            return
        publish("serve", {"event_type": "served"})
        if available[movie] < num_tickets:
            arguing = publish("argue", {"status": "started"})
            yield env.timeout(0.5)
            publish("argue", {"event_type": "argued"}, arguing)
            counter.release(turn)
            return
        publish("buy", {"event_type": "bought"})
        available[movie] -= num_tickets
        publish("check", {"event_type": "checked"})
        if available[movie] < 2:
            publish("sold", {"event_type": "sold_out", "movie": movie})
            sold_out[movie].succeed()
            available[movie] = 0
        finishing = publish("finish", {"status": "started"})
        yield env.timeout(1)
        publish("finish", {"event_type": "done"}, finishing)
        counter.release(turn)

    def customer_arrivals():
        for number in itertools.count(1):
            yield env.timeout(sampler.sample(gap))
            movie = MOVIES[int(movie_choices.integers(len(MOVIES)))]
            num_tickets = int(ticket_counts.integers(1, 7))
            env.process(moviegoer(f"goers-{number}", movie, num_tickets))

    env.process(customer_arrivals())


def run() -> None:
    """Runs 120 simulation seconds."""
    env = DynamicRealtimeEnvironment(factor=0)
    env.setup_egress([ConsoleEgress()])
    build(env)
    try:
        env.run(until=UNTIL)
    finally:
        env.teardown()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    run()

"""
Movie renege example

Covers:

- Resources: Resource
- Condition events
- Shared events

Scenario:
  A movie theatre has one ticket counter selling tickets for three
  movies (next show only). When a movie is sold out, all people waiting
  to buy tickets for that movie renege (leave queue).

"""

from __future__ import annotations

import random
from typing import Dict, List, NamedTuple, Optional

import simpy

RANDOM_SEED = 42
TICKETS = 50  # Number of tickets per movie
SELLOUT_THRESHOLD = 2  # Fewer tickets than this is a sellout
SIM_TIME = 120  # Simulate until


def moviegoer(env, movie, num_tickets, theater):
    """A moviegoer tries to by a number of tickets (*num_tickets*) for
    a certain *movie* in a *theater*.

    If the movie becomes sold out, she leaves the theater. If she gets
    to the counter, she tries to buy a number of tickets. If not enough
    tickets are left, she argues with the teller and leaves.

    If at most one ticket is left after the moviegoer bought her
    tickets, the *sold out* event for this movie is triggered causing
    all remaining moviegoers to leave.

    """
    with theater.counter.request() as my_turn:
        # Wait until it's our turn or until the movie is sold out
        result = yield my_turn | theater.sold_out[movie]

        # Check if it's our turn or if movie is sold out
        if my_turn not in result:
            theater.num_renegers[movie] += 1
            return

        # Check if enough tickets left.
        if theater.available[movie] < num_tickets:
            # Moviegoer leaves after some discussion
            yield env.timeout(0.5)
            return

        # Buy tickets
        theater.available[movie] -= num_tickets
        if theater.available[movie] < SELLOUT_THRESHOLD:
            # Trigger the "sold out" event for the movie
            theater.sold_out[movie].succeed()
            theater.when_sold_out[movie] = env.now
            theater.available[movie] = 0
        yield env.timeout(1)


def customer_arrivals(env, theater):
    """Create new *moviegoers* until the sim time reaches 120."""
    while True:
        yield env.timeout(random.expovariate(1 / 0.5))

        movie = random.choice(theater.movies)
        num_tickets = random.randint(1, 6)
        if theater.available[movie]:
            env.process(moviegoer(env, movie, num_tickets, theater))


class Theater(NamedTuple):
    counter: simpy.Resource
    movies: List[str]
    available: Dict[str, int]
    sold_out: Dict[str, simpy.Event]
    when_sold_out: Dict[str, Optional[float]]
    num_renegers: Dict[str, int]


# Setup and start the simulation
print('Movie renege')
random.seed(RANDOM_SEED)
env = simpy.Environment()

# Create movie theater
movies = ['Python Unchained', 'Kill Process', 'Pulp Implementation']
theater = Theater(
    counter=simpy.Resource(env, capacity=1),
    movies=movies,
    available=dict.fromkeys(movies, TICKETS),
    sold_out={movie: env.event() for movie in movies},
    when_sold_out=dict.fromkeys(movies),
    num_renegers=dict.fromkeys(movies, 0),
)

# Start process and run
env.process(customer_arrivals(env, theater))
env.run(until=SIM_TIME)

# Analysis/results
for movie in movies:
    if theater.sold_out[movie]:
        sellout_time = theater.when_sold_out[movie]
        num_renegers = theater.num_renegers[movie]
        print(
            f'Movie "{movie}" sold out {sellout_time:.1f} minutes '
            f'after ticket counter opening.'
        )
        print(f'  Number of people leaving queue when film sold out: {num_renegers}')

docs.title: Process Communication
docs.text: A generator puts messages into a pipe and a consumer takes them, first from one pipe and then from two. This is SimPy's Process Communication example, written in desflow.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text:
SimPy's example has a generator that puts a message into a store every 6 to 10 time units. The message holds the time it was sent. A consumer takes a message and then works on it for 4 to 8 time units, so it takes some messages late. The run lasts 100 time units. SimPy runs the example twice: once with one consumer (one to one), and once with two consumers that each have a pipe of their own, which the generator fills with a broadcast pipe (one to many). SimPy counts no unit, and desflow reads each unit as one second.

The example has two blueprints, process_communication.yaml for one to one and process_communication_broadcast.yaml for one to many, and a builder and a low-level file for each. desflow examples get downloads both.

The example needs only desflow, which each Quick Start in Run It installs, and no other service. desflow examples get simpy-process-communication --api yaml downloads it, as Get an Example shows. SimPy Examples says how these pages read SimPy's times and numbers. SimPy's own page for the example is on its documentation site.

docs.title: Generator Sends
docs.text:
SimPy's message_generator waits 6 to 10 time units and puts a message with the time it was sent into the pipe, without waiting for the put.

docs/snippets/simpy/process_communication.py:generator-sends
def message_generator(name, env, out_pipe):
    """A process which randomly generates messages."""
    while True:
        # wait for next transmission
        yield env.timeout(random.randint(6, 10))

        # messages are time stamped to later check if the consumer was
        # late getting them.  Note, using event.triggered to do this may
        # result in failure due to FIFO nature of simulation yields.
        # (i.e. if at the same env.now, message_generator puts a message
        # in the pipe first and then message_consumer gets from pipe,
        # the event.triggered will be True in the other order it will be
        # False
        msg = (env.now, f'{name} says hello at {env.now}')
        out_pipe.put(msg)

docs.title: Consumer Gets
docs.text:
SimPy's message_consumer takes a message from the pipe, prints it, and works on it for 4 to 8 time units. It is late for a message that was sent before it asked for it.

docs/snippets/simpy/process_communication.py:consumer-gets
def message_consumer(name, env, in_pipe):
    """A process which consumes messages."""
    while True:
        # Get event for message pipe
        msg = yield in_pipe.get()

        if msg[0] < env.now:
            # if message was already put into pipe, then
            # message_consumer was late getting to it. Depending on what
            # is being modeled this, may, or may not have some
            # significance
            print(
                f'LATE Getting Message: at time {env.now}: '
                f'{name} received message: {msg[1]}'
            )

        else:
            # message_consumer is synchronized with message_generator
            print(f'at time {env.now}: {name} received message: {msg[1]}.')

        # Process does some other work, which may result in missing messages
        yield env.timeout(random.randint(4, 8))

docs.title: Broadcast Pipe
docs.text:
SimPy's BroadcastPipe keeps one store for each consumer and puts each message into all of them.

docs/snippets/simpy/process_communication.py:broadcast-pipe
class BroadcastPipe:
    """A Broadcast pipe that allows one process to send messages to many.

    This construct is useful when message consumers are running at
    different rates than message generators and provides an event
    buffering to the consuming processes.

    The parameters are used to create a new
    :class:`~simpy.resources.store.Store` instance each time
    :meth:`get_output_conn()` is called.

    """

    def __init__(self, env, capacity=simpy.core.Infinity):
        self.env = env
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.pipes = []

    def put(self, value):
        """Broadcast a *value* to all receivers."""
        if not self.pipes:
            raise RuntimeError('There are no output pipes.')
        events = [store.put(value) for store in self.pipes]
        return self.env.all_of(events)  # Condition event for all "events"

    def get_output_conn(self):
        """Get a new output connection for this broadcast pipe.

        The return value is a :class:`~simpy.resources.store.Store`.

        """
        pipe = simpy.Store(self.env, capacity=self.capacity)
        self.pipes.append(pipe)
        return pipe

class BroadcastPipe:
    """A pipe that puts each message into the store of every consumer."""

    def __init__(self, env: DynamicRealtimeEnvironment):
        self.env = env
        self.pipes: list = []

    def put(self, value):
        """Puts `value` into every output store."""
        return self.env.all_of([pipe.put(value) for pipe in self.pipes])

    def get_output_conn(self):
        """A new store that receives every message from now on."""
        pipe = simpy.Store(self.env)
        self.pipes.append(pipe)
        return pipe

docs.title: Check the Result
docs.text:
In the one to one run the generator sends 13 messages in the 100 seconds, and the consumer receives 12. The first message is sent at 8 seconds and received at once. The consumer finishes 11 of them. No message is late: the consumer is free each time one of the first 12 messages is sent, so it takes each one at once. The 13th message is sent at 99 seconds, while the consumer is still working on the 12th, so it is not taken before the run ends.

In the one to many run the generator also sends 13 messages, and each consumer receives 12. No receipt is late. SimPy prints one line for each message taken, and its output for the one to one run is shown below. desflow draws each random value from its own stream, named by the place where the value is used, such as arrivals.generator.gap. A seed of 42 therefore gives different numbers from SimPy's random.seed(42). The system is the same. The figures are not.

# Process Communication: SimPy's process_communication.py example, one to one, in YAML.
#
# The YAML version of process_communication_example.py, which --api builder downloads.
# A generator puts a message into a store every 6 to 10 seconds, stamped with the time
# it was sent. A consumer takes each message and then works on it for 4 to 8 seconds,
# so it is late for some messages: `late` is true when the message waited in the store.
# process_communication_broadcast.yaml sends each message to two consumers.
#
# Each value is drawn from desflow's random sequence for its place in the file, so the
# numbers differ from those SimPy prints.
#
# Needs no containers. Runs unpaced and ends after 100 simulation seconds.
# Run it from its folder with: desflow run process_communication.yaml

simulation: {sim_id: Pipes, factor: 0, random_seed: 42}

egress:
  - {type: Console}

stores:
  pipe: {}

arrivals:
  generator:
    gap: {gen: integer, bounds: [6, 10]}
    spawn: speak
  consumer: {initial: 1, spawn: listen}

tasks:
  speak:
    payload: {event_type: said}
    # The generator does not wait for its put, as SimPy's `out_pipe.put(msg)` does not
    put:
      store: pipe
      wait: false
      item:
        sent: {gen: expr, expr: t}
        text:
          gen: format
          template: "Generator A says hello at {now:g}"
          names:
            now: {gen: expr, expr: t}

    payload:
      event_type: received
      late: {gen: expr, expr: "item.sent < t"}
      text: {gen: expr, expr: "item.text"}
